entries.title: Go, Python and Rust extensions: in a `before_agent_start` handler, the event's `systemPrompt` and the…
entries.symptom: Go, Python and Rust extensions: in a `before_agent_start` handler, the event's `systemPrompt` and the context's system prompt getter now return the prompt the shared options render when read, as Pi and Node do.
entries.rootCause: Each SDK now holds the prompt the host rendered for the options the handler received and, once the options differ, asks the host to render them with renderSystemPrompt, reusing the result until they change again: - Go: data["systemPrompt"] is an *sdk.SystemPrompt (Get, MarshalJSON), since a map cannot run a getter; ctx.GetSystemPrompt() returns the same value. - Python: the event dict's "systemPrompt" and ctx.get_system_prompt() render. The Host answers renderSystemPrompt without a UI bridge too (an SDK session): the render is a pure function of the options the call carries. Callers of the Go string form move to Get(); the known gaps are deleted; pig-go.json is regenerated by gointerfaces.
entries.releaseNote: Go, Python and Rust extensions: in a `before_agent_start` handler, the event's `systemPrompt` and the context's system prompt getter now return the prompt the shared options render when read, as Pi and Node do. A handler sees its own edit to `systemPromptOptions` at once, a later handler sees it, and after a handler returns `systemPrompt` later handlers read exactly that prompt; before, they read the prompt rendered before the handler ran, and the context getter returned the Session's prompt.

entries.releaseNote: A session message whose members are in another order than Pi writes them, or that holds members PiG does not model, now reaches RPC `get_messages`, extension events and the built session context exactly as Pi returns it: the object parsed from the file, written with `JSON.stringify`. Context edits and handler replacements without content keep the content member in place, as the JavaScript spread does. A system message without content is kept and gets empty content, as in Pi; before, PiG dropped it. Messages Pi wrote are unaffected and retain no extra memory.

entries.userImpact: An operation failed or was rejected
entries.releaseNote: A Provider object registered by an extension (`pi.registerProvider(provider)`) now receives the session's `onResponse` and `onProviderStreamEvent` callbacks in its stream options, as in Pi, so `after_provider_response` and `provider_stream_event` fire for its requests. entries.releaseNote: Key matching follows Pi for three terminal inputs. An unmodified letter, digit or symbol binding no longer matches a modifyOtherKeys sequence.

entries.title: fix(extension): hold the theme colors map the wire palette memo is keyed on
entries.symptom: fix(extension): hold the theme colors map the wire palette memo is keyed on
entries.rootCause: ActiveExtensionThemeWire identified the terminal-resolved colors by the address of the map theme.Colors returned, stored as a uintptr. The theme drops that map when the terminal's reported colors change, so the collector could free it and give its address to a later colors map with other values; the memo would then return the old palette and the state push would skip the theme as unchanged. The memo now holds the map it is keyed on, so the address cannot be reused while it identifies the palette.

entries.title: In print and JSON mode, Node extensions in separate processes now keep Pi's order when a later extension's…
entries.symptom: In print and JSON mode, Node extensions in separate processes now keep Pi's order when a later extension's `session_shutdown` or `agent_settled` handler awaits a timer, however busy the machine is.
entries.rootCause: an ordering assumption, not a lost frame. Pi runs every extension on one event loop, so while the later handler awaits its timer the immediate and the due timer the earlier handler queued run first, whatever the OS does (runner.ts:1096-1123). With separate Node processes the yielding runtime sent loop_turned and went on at once ("Nothing waits for the notify"), so the earlier process's callbacks ran before the later handler's continuation only if that process was scheduled, read the forwarded turn, and reached its check and timers phases within the later handler's 100 ms timer. On a loaded host it was not: the later handler answered first, the host invalidated, and the earlier callbacks ran…
entries.releaseNote: In print and JSON mode, Node extensions in separate processes now keep Pi's order when a later extension's `session_shutdown` or `agent_settled` handler awaits a timer, however busy the machine is. The immediate and the timer an earlier extension's handler queued ran before that handler resumed only if the earlier process read the forwarded `loop_turned` in time; a process the OS kept waiting ran them after the handler answered, with a stale ctx once the runner was invalidated. The yielding process now stays in its turn until every other Node process reports it took the turn (`loop_turn_taken`), after the immediates and due timers it queued before the turn ran.

entries.title: `String.prototype.trim` vs `strings.TrimSpace`: four Pi `.trim()` sites used Go's `strings.TrimSpace`, which…
entries.symptom: `String.prototype.trim` vs `strings.TrimSpace`: four Pi `.trim()` sites used Go's `strings.TrimSpace`, which trims U+0085 and not U+FEFF where JavaScript trims U+FEFF and not U+0085 (`jsstring.Trim` is the JS rule, already used in 100 other places).
entries.userImpact: An operation failed or was rejected
entries.releaseNote: `String.prototype.trim` vs `strings.TrimSpace`: four Pi `.trim()` sites used Go's `strings.TrimSpace`, which trims U+0085 and not U+FEFF where JavaScript trims U+FEFF and not U+0085 (`jsstring.Trim` is the JS rule, already used in 100 other places). Fixed where the difference is observable: `Text` blank check (`tui/text.go`, text.ts:57), assistant-message text/thinking runs (`tui/assistant_message_block.go`, assistant-message.ts:110-125: a leading BOM is now trimmed before the markdown renders, U+0085 is kept), replayed empty-thinking filter (`agent/transform.go`, transform-messages.ts:111) and the proxy `data:` line (`agent/proxy.go`, proxy.ts:181). Regressions `TestTextBlankCheckTrimsLikeJavaScript`, `TestAssistantMessageComponentTrimsRunsLikeJavaScript`, `TestReplayAndProxyLinesTrimLikeJavaScript` (each red with the old call, 3 sites checked by swapping the call back). `parseStreamingJsonValue`'s guard (`ai/streaming_json.go`) was probed and left: the result is the same either way. Left for owners: `stripThinkingSignatures` (`ai/anthropic.go`, PiG's own D37 recovery, no Pi counterpart), the Pi `.trim()` sites in other providers if any still use `TrimSpace`. `./tui -race` (1,219 s) failed only the flaky `TestSurfaceRendersAnEditorBeforeAnythingAsksForItsTerminal` (race in `tui_surface_program_status_test.go:213`, passes alone) and `./agent` only `TestAgentClassMatchesPi`/`TestAgentLoopMatchesPi` (the oracle cannot import `@earendil-works/pi-ai` from `durable/interop`, a missing node_modules in this worktree).

entries.title: Bug report files against live Pi: new `TestBugReportFilesMatchPi`…
entries.symptom: Bug report files against live Pi: new `TestBugReportFilesMatchPi` (`internal/codingagent/bug_report_files_oracle_test.go`; `collectBugReportDiagnostics` over a `SessionManager` opened on 500 generated session files plus a crash log, and `bugReportFiles`; bytes of diagnostics.json, member list, session.jsonl and summary.md).

Two real fixes, both red first (128 of 500, then 13): (1) report.json and diagnostics.json went through `json.Encoder`, which writes U+2028/U+2029 as `\u2028` where `JSON.stringify` writes them literally (and kept Go number text); `bugReportJSON` now canonicalises through `stringifyIndented` (`internal/codingagent/bug_report.go`); (2) a diagnostic's `details: {}` was dropped by `omitempty` (`ai.AssistantMessageDiagnostic` now has a `MarshalJSON` that keeps an empty, non-nil Details; regression `TestAssistantMessageDiagnosticKeepsAnEmptyDetailsObject`). 14 mutations red (crash `notified` strip needed the crash corpus to be a JSON array, as `readCrashLog` expects). Findings left for a ruling (questions/lg-help-4.md): PiG's `AssistantMessage` cannot tell an empty `errorMessage`/`rawStopReason` from an absent one (Pi keeps `""`), and a diagnostic's `details` is a Go map, so non-index key order is sorted, not insertion order; both are excluded from the corpus and named in the test comment. Not compared: report.json content (metadata tests), the zip container (Pi writes a classic layout, Go's archive/zip a data-descriptor layout; the members' content is what a reader sees).

entries.title: Provider error text is written the way Pi writes it
entries.symptom: Provider error text is written the way Pi writes it.
entries.rootCause: It found two differences in Pig, fixed here: - SafeJsonStringify wrote encoding/json text: U+2028 and U+2029 escaped, -0 as -0, integer-like keys sorted lexically. JSON.stringify writes them raw, 0, and integer keys first. It now passes the encoded text through jsonstringify.Canonicalize (JSON.parse then stringify of validated JSON, which keeps lone surrogates), so raw provider bodies (json.RawMessage) and decoded values give Pi's text. - truncateUTF16 (slice(0, limit)) dropped the first half of a surrogate pair when the cut fell inside it; JavaScript keeps the lone high surrogate, U+FFFD once encoded as UTF-8. It now keeps U+FFFD. Callers: TruncateErrorText, the Radius gateway text cap and…
entries.userImpact: An operation failed or was rejected
entries.releaseNote: Provider error text is written the way Pi writes it. A JSON error body keeps U+2028 and U+2029 as they are instead of `\u2028`, writes `-0` as `0`, keeps lone surrogates, and lists integer-like keys first (`JSON.stringify` rules). Text that is cut to a length limit (error bodies, Radius gateway text, Pi message text) keeps a replacement character where the cut falls inside an emoji or other pair of UTF-16 units, as Pi's `slice` leaves half of the pair, instead of dropping the half.

entries.title: PiG, the extension SDKs and the sprite selection use one configuration root: `PIG_HOME`, else…
entries.symptom: PiG, the extension SDKs and the sprite selection use one configuration root: `PIG_HOME`, else `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/pig`, else `~/.pig`.
entries.rootCause: Pi's JsonRevisionValidator validates object properties in Reflect.ownKeys order and throws the first failing property's TypeError (revision-validator.ts:26-33). So a state with several invalid properties always reports the same error. Go's normalize walked the map in random order, so Prepare's error changed from run to run. Example: NaN at a and a struct at b gave either 'non-finite number' or 'containers must be plain objects'.
entries.userImpact: An operation failed or was rejected
entries.releaseNote: PiG, the extension SDKs and the sprite selection use one configuration root: `PIG_HOME`, else `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/pig`, else `~/.pig`. The Python SDK's `config_home` ignored `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, the Rust SDK's `config_home` still read the retired `GOPI_HOME`, and the Go SDK, the sprite selection and several host paths each had their own copy of the rule, so an extension could read or write a different directory than the CLI. An empty `PIG_HOME` or `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` now falls through to the next choice, a leading `~` or `~/` expands to your home directory everywhere, and any other value is used as written. If the configuration root needs your home directory and PiG cannot find it, PiG reports an error and exits (`pig --version` and other commands that need no root still run) instead of writing under a path relative to the working directory. Pi-sharing mode (`PIG_USE_PI_DIRS=1`) still moves only the agent and project directories, so a fresh `pig` in that mode writes its documentation and stages the extension SDKs under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/pig`. Reported by @baggiiiie (#200).

entries.rootCause: box.ts addChild, removeChild and clear call only invalidateCache, which drops the box's own cache. Pi invalidates the children only from Box.invalidate. Go's Box.AddChild, RemoveChild and Clear called b.Invalidate(), which also invalidates every child. It reports it on stderr and still disposes.

entries.title: Session lines (and every other JSON.stringify-mode encode) now write ill-formed UTF-8 the way Pi does: one…
entries.symptom: PiG used to write one `\ufffd` escape per bad byte, so `"a\xe2\x82b"` became `"a\ufffd\ufffdb"` where Pi writes `"a�b"`.
entries.rootCause: JSON.stringify of a string decoded from ill-formed UTF-8 writes one raw U+FFFD per WHATWG maximal subpart; PiG's session lines wrote one \ufffd escape per bad byte. The codec now counts one replacement per maximal subpart in every mode, writes it raw in the JSON.stringify mode, and rewrites nested \ufffd escapes to raw there. Marshal and MarshalJS keep the escape form. Session files written before keep their form and read back the same.
entries.releaseNote: Session lines (and every other JSON.stringify-mode encode) now write ill-formed UTF-8 the way Pi does: one raw U+FFFD per WHATWG maximal subpart (what a JavaScript string decoded from those bytes holds, and what JSON.stringify writes). PiG used to write one `\ufffd` escape per bad byte, so `"a\xe2\x82b"` became `"a\ufffd\ufffdb"` where Pi writes `"a�b"`. Nested `\ufffd` escapes from PiG's own types are written raw as well. Session files written before this change keep the old form and read back the same strings. On the extension wire (the codec's `Marshal`/`MarshalJS`), ill-formed UTF-8 also counts one replacement per maximal subpart rather than per byte; the `\ufffd` escape form there is unchanged.

entries.rootCause: Pi's RPC signal handler kills tracked children and awaits runtimeHost.dispose on its one event loop (rpc-mode.ts:366-376,726-744). PiG's run went on concurrently: with a throwing handler it persisted the tool result and an assistant turn and sent a second provider request before exiting. RPC mode now registers the same termination prelude as print mode: Session.HoldAgentEvents from the moment the signal arrives until a handler reports its yield or the Session is disposed.

entries.title: `pig package publish --to npm` and `pig piglet publish --to npm` no longer run an `npm` that the published…
entries.symptom: Windows' `cmd.exe` could pick a Package's own `npm.cmd` ahead of the author's npm, and a relative `npmCommand` was resolved inside the Package directory.
entries.rootCause: The bash tool on Windows puts the shell in a job object. When the shell exits, `processGroupMayHoldOutput` asks Windows whether the job still has processes (`QueryInformationJobObject`, `JobObjectBasicAccountingInformation`). If the answer is zero, `childwait.waitIdle` waits for the output pipe to reach EOF with no further bound, because an empty job means no process can still hold the pipe.
entries.releaseNote: `pig package publish --to npm` and `pig piglet publish --to npm` no longer run an `npm` that the published directory contains. PiG finds npm in the absolute directories on `PATH`, so publishing from inside a Package that ships its own `npm` works and uses your npm (or resolves a relative `npmCommand` against the directory you run `pig` in) and starts that file. Before, Windows' `cmd.exe` could pick a Package's own `npm.cmd` ahead of the author's npm, and a relative `npmCommand` was resolved inside the Package directory.

entries.title: In print and JSON mode, an extension in its own Node process no longer runs its callbacks with a stale ctx…
entries.symptom: In print and JSON mode, an extension in its own Node process no longer runs its callbacks with a stale ctx when a later extension's handler awaits a timer or I/O.
entries.rootCause: Pi's runner awaits each extension's handler in turn on one event loop (runner.ts:1089-1116). When a later extension's session_shutdown or agent_settled handler awaits a timer or I/O, that loop runs the immediate or timer an earlier extension's handler queued, with a live ctx, before print mode invalidates the runner (agent-session-runtime.ts:404-410, agent-session.ts:1393-1406). With isolated Node processes the earlier process waited for the host's next step after answering (), so its callbacks ran only after invalidate, or never, because the host stopped the process first. Packed processes share one loop and matched Pi.
entries.userImpact: An operation failed or was rejected
entries.releaseNote: In print and JSON mode, an extension in its own Node process no longer runs its callbacks with a stale ctx when a later extension's handler awaits a timer or I/O. Pi runs every extension on one event loop, so the immediate or timer that one extension's `session_shutdown` or `agent_settled` handler queues runs while the next extension's handler waits, before the runner is invalidated. The Node runtime now reports such a wait with a `loop_turned` notification, which the host forwards to every other Node process as its next step. Packed extensions already shared one loop and behave as before; RPC and interactive mode are unchanged.

entries.title: On arm64 and other CPUs with a fused multiply-add, the OKHSL saturation of a color (used when generating the…
entries.symptom: It differed from Pi's in the last bit for about 9% of sRGB colors.
entries.rootCause: rgbToOkhsl assigns k1 := 0.8 * c0 and adds it in k1 + (1 - k1/cMid) * chroma. Assigning a product does not round it in Go: on arm64 the compiler fused 0.8 * c0 into that addition (FMADD), so ColorToOkhsl's saturation, which the system theme generator reads, differed from Pi's oklab.ts:225-226 in the last bit for 1523533 of the 16.7M sRGB colors (633339 of those then match Pi exactly; the others differ from Pi through Go's Pow/Cbrt/Atan2 as well).
entries.releaseNote: On arm64 and other CPUs with a fused multiply-add, the OKHSL saturation of a color (used when generating the system theme's colors) rounds `0.8 * c0` before adding it, as Pi does. Before, it differed from Pi's in the last bit for about 9% of sRGB colors.

entries.title: The crash notice prints the year of a crash time the way Node's toLocaleString does: unpadded, and counted…
entries.symptom: The crash notice prints the year of a crash time the way Node's toLocaleString does: unpadded, and counted back from 1 for years before 1 CE.
entries.rootCause: interactive-mode.ts:1222 prints `new Date(crash.timestamp).toLocaleString()`. The Go notice used the layout "1/2/2006, 3:04:05 PM", whose year is zero padded to four digits and signed before 1 CE; en-US toLocaleString prints the Gregorian era year unpadded and, before 1 CE, counted back from 1 without a sign ("4/15/151", "10/13/1721" for 1721 BCE). enUSDateTime now builds the string. A crash record's year is the current one in practice, so this shows only for a forged or damaged record. The locale stays en-US: Node uses the process locale (LANG=de_DE gives "31.12.1969, 16:00:00"), which is not modelled and not recorded as a divergence pending the owner.
entries.releaseNote: The crash notice prints the year of a crash time the way Node's toLocaleString does: unpadded, and counted back from 1 for years before 1 CE.

entries.title: Tool schemas in OpenAI Completions, OpenAI Responses, Codex and Mistral request bodies keep the members in…

entries.rootCause: Pi passes a tool's parameters object through to the body (openai-completions.ts convertTools :1506-1514, openai-responses-shared.ts :386-390), so JSON.stringify writes the schema's members in declaration order; a strict schema is the same object rebuilt member by member (constrained-sampling.ts makeJsonSchemaNodeStrict: required, then additionalProperties are assigned after the existing members, and an optional property becomes {anyOf: [property, {type: "null"}]}). entries.releaseNote: Tool schemas in OpenAI Completions, OpenAI Responses, Codex and Mistral request bodies keep the members in the order the tool declares them. Strict schemas add `required` and then `additionalProperties`, as Pi does. `cache_control` comes after the members of the tool or text part that carries it.

entries.symptom: The Piglet JSON Schema that `pig piglet schema` prints rejected `powershell` in `tools`, which `pig piglet validate` accepts as a built-in tool, and stated nothing for most of the other closed vocabulary.
entries.rootCause: The schema listed seven built-in tools while the parser accepts eight, so it rejected a Piglet that used powershell. With a focused custom overlay, tui.ts:598-665 records the dialog as blocking the overlay's focus restore and, once the hidden dialog is unmounted, resumes the overlay, so the custom overlay has focus and the next key again. An editor-slot custom component is cleared out of the slot by the dialog, so focus goes to the editor. The custom component receives no input while the dialog is up. Before, a subprocess extension's dialog waited until the custom component closed. A dialog from an in-process extension opened at once, but the custom component kept focus, and a subprocess custom component kept reading the keys meant for the dialog.

entries.title: A Piglet Binary with a fused Go extension starts within a few milliseconds of Stock PiG
entries.symptom: A Piglet Binary with a fused Go extension starts within a few milliseconds of Stock PiG.
entries.rootCause: A Piglet Binary with one fused Go extension took 72.1 ms for -p with the faux provider against 31.7 ms for Stock PiG. The extension host encoded the whole model catalog (more than 1 MB of JSON) three times while it wired model operations and sent it to every extension, though the Go, Rust and Python SDKs answer ctx.modelRegistry with a blocking getModelRegistryState call and discard the snapshot.
entries.releaseNote: A Piglet Binary with a fused Go extension starts within a few milliseconds of Stock PiG. On an Apple M4 Pro (median of 20, faux provider), `-p` took 72.1 ms against 31.7 ms for Stock PiG and now takes 33.0 ms, and the first typed key showed in the editor after 71.0 ms against 33.6 ms and now after 33.4 ms. The extension host encoded the whole model catalog (more than 1 MB of JSON) three times at startup for every extension. Now it builds and sends that snapshot only to Node extensions, which answer `ctx.modelRegistry` reads from it. Go, Rust and Python extensions read the registry from the host when they ask, as before, so Stock PiG with such extensions starts faster too. See D19 in `docs/additive-features.md`.

entries.title: Ill-formed UTF-8 in a string that PiG re-encodes as JSON (an extension's raw JSON, tool schemas, code-mode…
entries.symptom: Ill-formed UTF-8 in a string that PiG re-encodes as JSON (an extension's raw JSON, tool schemas, code-mode keys, Bedrock and Google request members) is written as `JSON.stringify` writes the decoded text: one literal U+FFFD for each ill-formed sequence, instead of one `\ufffd` escape per byte.
entries.rootCause: Design step 1 ("internal/jsnumber.String, jsstring and jsonstringify's string writer become callers"): - internal/jsstring.AppendString is jsparity.AppendString. It was an ASCII fast path plus MarshalJSON through the SDK encoder. - internal/jsnumber.String writes finite numbers with jsparity.AppendNumber instead of a safe-integer branch plus json.Marshal. - internal/jsonstringify's canonicalize writes numbers with jsparity.AppendNumber. stringToken is JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(token)): jv.Parse decodes to WTF-8 and jsparity.AppendString writes it, replacing a hand-written escape rewriter.
entries.releaseNote: Ill-formed UTF-8 in a string that PiG re-encodes as JSON (an extension's raw JSON, tool schemas, code-mode keys, Bedrock and Google request members) is written as `JSON.stringify` writes the decoded text: one literal U+FFFD for each ill-formed sequence, instead of one `\ufffd` escape per byte.

entries.title: A terminal's reply to the startup color query now applies the colors and ends the startup wait before the…

entries.rootCause: Pi settles the color query inside the input handler, and its .then(apply) and the await continuation run as microtasks before the next input chunk. The owner loop now receives the query's completion itself: the input that completes the query applies its colors before it returns, a task posted at the timeout applies a timed-out query, and the startup color wait returns before it reads more input once the latest query applied.

A prompt typed right after the terminal answered, for example by a client that types as soon as the editor shows, reaches the ordinary submit handler instead of reporting "Startup is still in progress".

entries.title: A running `!command` that prints a lot, the `/resume` search over many long sessions, and streamed answers…
entries.symptom: A running `!command` that prints a lot, the `/resume` search over many long sessions, and streamed answers without Mermaid diagrams cost less per frame or keystroke, with the same output.
entries.rootCause: Each keystroke in /resume's search rebuilt every session's search text (id, name, all message text, cwd) and lowered and converted it to UTF-16 for each fuzzy token, so a keystroke allocated several copies of all text of all sessions. Pi does the same (session-selector-search.ts getSessionSearchText per match, fuzzyMatch lowers the text). The selector now keeps, per listed session, the search text with the forms the query modes read: the lowercase UTF-16 units for fuzzy tokens, the whitespace-normalized lowercase text for phrases, and the unit runes for regex. Each form is prepared when a query first needs it.
entries.releaseNote: A running `!command` that prints a lot, the `/resume` search over many long sessions, and streamed answers without Mermaid diagrams cost less per frame or keystroke, with the same output.

entries.title: A finished code-mode execution no longer keeps its closed VM reachable through its stopped halt-grace timer…
entries.symptom: A finished code-mode execution no longer keeps its closed VM reachable through its stopped halt-grace timer, which stays in an idle scheduler's timer heap until that scheduler next runs.
entries.rootCause: The end RSS moved in 64 MiB steps (the bytes each script touches), which looked like the runtime returning pages late. It is not: wazero runs here without a custom allocator, so a VM's linear memory is one Go heap slice reserved at the heap limit plus 64 MiB of headroom (320 MiB), and the live Go heap after runtime.GC() was 0 to 6 of those above the start. A closed VM was still reachable.
entries.releaseNote: A finished code-mode execution no longer keeps its closed VM reachable through its stopped halt-grace timer, which stays in an idle scheduler's timer heap until that scheduler next runs. Each such VM held its whole linear memory (the heap limit plus 64 MiB, 320 MiB at a 256 MiB limit) until then. After 16 concurrent executions on a 196-CPU Linux host, the live Go heap after a collection was 0 to 6 of those memories above the start before the fix (up to 1.9 GiB) and under 0.1 MiB after it.

entries.title: Chord host timers (reload vote, gate and retire deadlines, link pings, service linger, host manager grace…
entries.symptom: A deadline above the limit used to never fire and a zero one fired at once.
entries.rootCause: Pi's chord timers are Node timers: lib/internal/timers.js Timeout runs a delay outside [1, TIMEOUT_MAX = 2^31-1] ms after 1 ms, and insert truncates the rest to whole milliseconds. The Go port handed the raw Duration to time.AfterFunc/NewTimer/NewTicker, so a deadline above TIMEOUT_MAX never fired, a zero or negative one fired at once, and fractions were kept.
entries.releaseNote: Chord host timers (reload vote, gate and retire deadlines, link pings, service linger, host manager grace, ready timeout and keepAlive interval) wait as Node's `setTimeout` does: a delay above 2147483647 ms, below 1 ms or zero runs after 1 ms, and fractional milliseconds are truncated. A deadline above the limit used to never fire and a zero one fired at once.

entries.title: fix(ai): an iteration's shared cancellation does not compare contexts
entries.symptom: fix(ai): an iteration's shared cancellation does not compare contexts
entries.rootCause: An earlier change's one-registration-per-iteration path compared the iterator's recorded context with the context of each later next() using ==. Go panics when it compares two interface values whose identical dynamic type is not comparable, so Events(ctx) with a context struct carrying a slice or map (passed by value) panicked at its second wait: "comparing uncomparable type". Both iteration loops (events() turn path, observeEvents) pass the same captured context to every next(), so the comparison never decided anything. The registration is now armed once, keyed on stop == nil, and contexts are not compared.

entries.rootCause: streamable-http.ts:163 matches /(?:^|[\s,])error="?insufficient_scope"?/i and flow.ts:197 asks for consent when scope.split(/\s+/) includes offline_access. JavaScript's \s includes U+00A0, U+FEFF and the Unicode spaces and excludes U+0085; RE2's \s is ASCII only and strings.Fields splits at U+0085 and not at U+FEFF. A 403 whose challenge separated the field with a no-break space was not treated as step-up authorization, and a scope joined with a BOM or ending in U+0085 got the wrong prompt. The regex now uses the JS class (as mcp/oauth/discovery.go already does) and StartAuthorization uses scopeFields (as flow.go:553 already does).

entries.title: `auth.json` keeps each credential's properties in the order they were read or returned by an extension's…

entries.rootCause: BenchmarkCredentialKeyOrderRoundTrip decodes and encodes an auth.json of three credentials. The remaining cost is the default encoding that decides whether an order must be kept. That cost is acceptable, because AuthStorage decodes only when auth.json's revision changes and encodes only on a login, refresh or logout.
entries.releaseNote: `auth.json` keeps each credential's properties in the order they were read or returned by an extension's login, as Pi keeps the object it stores and writes it with `JSON.stringify`. Before, PiG rewrote every credential in a fixed key order whenever `auth.json` was saved, including credentials of providers that were not changed. A `config.oauth` login's credential gets its `type` after the flow's own properties, as Pi's `{ ...credential, type: "oauth" }` does. A credential that one of PiG's built-in logins creates still uses PiG's own key order, not the order of Pi's object literal.

entries.title: Pressing a key in a subprocess extension's overlay no longer freezes interactive mode when the key reaches…
entries.symptom: Pressing a key in a subprocess extension's overlay no longer freezes interactive mode when the key reaches the overlay on the main loop (public PR #197).
entries.rootCause: The subprocess bridge reads a focused overlay's state before it forwards a key. That read queued a task on the owner loop and waited for its result, so a key delivered on the owner loop waited for work only that loop could run. Pi reads the same state synchronously on its single event loop. The owner loop is now identified by goroutine: a caller already on it runs owner work inline, and a post to its own full queue no longer blocks.
entries.releaseNote: Pressing a key in a subprocess extension's overlay no longer freezes interactive mode when the key reaches the overlay on the main loop (public PR #197).

The check now follows the intercept. TestInteractiveMode_EscapeClosesAutocompleteDuringCompactionWithoutAborting is red on the old order.

entries.title: In print and JSON mode, Node extensions that share one process now keep Pi's order at disposal
entries.symptom: An earlier extension's queued callback could run before a later extension's `session_shutdown` handler started, or a timer could run with a live ctx after the runner was invalidated, depending on the order in which the process read its sockets.
entries.rootCause: Pi's runner awaits each extension's handler in turn on one event loop (runner.ts:1089-1116). When a later extension's session_shutdown or agent_settled handler awaits a timer or I/O, that loop runs the immediate or timer an earlier extension's handler queued, with a live ctx, before print mode invalidates the runner (agent-session-runtime.ts:404-410, agent-session.ts:1393-1406). With isolated Node processes the earlier process waited for the host's next step after answering (), so its callbacks ran only after invalidate, or never, because the host stopped the process first. Packed processes share one loop and matched Pi.
entries.releaseNote: In print and JSON mode, Node extensions that share one process now keep Pi's order at disposal. Before, an earlier extension's queued callback could run before a later extension's `session_shutdown` handler started, or a timer could run with a live ctx after the runner was invalidated, depending on the order in which the process read its sockets.

entries.symptom: fix(extension): hold the theme colors map the wire palette memo is keyed on
entries.rootCause: ActiveExtensionThemeWire identified the terminal-resolved colors by the address of the map theme.Colors returned, stored as a uintptr. entries.title: An extension that a child agent session's resource loader loads now receives the session's events, as in Pi…
entries.symptom: An extension that a child agent session's resource loader loads now receives the session's events, as in Pi, where `createAgentSession` over a `DefaultResourceLoader` that loads an extension gives it `session_start` (after `bindExtensions`), `input`, `before_agent_start`, `agent_start`, `turn_*`, `message_*`, `context` and `agent_end`.
entries.rootCause: A DefaultResourceLoader loaded its extensions under the context of the reload that asked for them. A child agent session is created, and its loader reloaded, inside the wire call of createAgentSession, so the host stopped every extension the loader had loaded when that call returned: the extension had registered its tools and then received no event. The loader now owns the extensions it loaded until its next load or Close, as Pi's reload() has no caller whose end stops them; the context of the reload still ends the load itself.
entries.userImpact: An operation failed or was rejected
entries.releaseNote: An extension that a child agent session's resource loader loads now receives the session's events, as in Pi, where `createAgentSession` over a `DefaultResourceLoader` that loads an extension gives it `session_start` (after `bindExtensions`), `input`, `before_agent_start`, `agent_start`, `turn_*`, `message_*`, `context` and `agent_end`. In the Go, Python and Rust SDKs (through the `resources` option or a `resourceLoader` handle) the extension registered its tools and then received nothing: the loader started its extensions under the context of the call that reloaded it, which ends when `createAgentSession` returns, so the host stopped every extension it had just loaded and reported no error. The loader now owns its extensions until its next load or `Close`; the context of a reload still ends the reload itself.

entries.title: A start could fail with a bare missing-file error when another `pig`'s cache collection removed the cached…
entries.symptom: A start could fail with a bare missing-file error when another `pig`'s cache collection removed the cached extension build it had just reused.
entries.userImpact: An operation failed or was rejected
entries.releaseNote: A start could fail with a bare missing-file error when another `pig`'s cache collection removed the cached extension build it had just reused. The collection (the daily automatic one, or `pig extensions cache prune`) decides which entries are expired and removes them a moment later. A start that reuses an old entry in between refreshed its use time but holds no lease until its extension process spawns, so the entry was removed under it, the lease then came back empty instead of failing, and the spawn reported a missing file. The collection now reads each entry again under its exclusive lock and skips one that another `pig` used since, counting it as in use. A reuse takes the entry's lock while it checks and records the entry, so it never reuses an entry that is being removed and builds it again instead. A lease for an entry that is gone fails with `cache_lease_failed` and says the entry was removed. The SDK fingerprint file of a published entry is replaced through a rename and written only when it changes, so a collection can no longer read it half written and expire a build that a start is using.

entries.title: A Go or Rust extension edited while it was being built could be cached under the hash of the source from…
entries.symptom: A Go or Rust extension edited while it was being built could be cached under the hash of the source from before the edit.
entries.userImpact: An operation failed or was rejected
entries.releaseNote: A Go or Rust extension edited while it was being built could be cached under the hash of the source from before the edit. The compiler reads the source after the build hashed it, past the wait for another `pig`'s build of the same extension and through its own compile, and nothing read it again, so an edit saved in that time was compiled into a build stored under the original source's hash. Putting the original source back then ran the build of the edit. A build now reads its inputs again when the compiler returns (the extension source, the SDK, workspace modules and toolchain) and caches nothing when they changed: it fails with `changed while it was being built`, and the next start builds the current source. A Rust crate's `Cargo.lock`, which `cargo` writes during the build, does not count as an edit.

entries.symptom: A Node extension that registers or unregisters a provider through `ctx.modelRegistry` (or `pi.registerProvider`/`unregisterProvider`) sees the write on the next line, as Pi does: `find`, `getAll`, `getAvailable`, `hasConfiguredAuth`, `getProviderAuthStatus` and `isUsingOAuth` read the registry the registration left, and an unregistration removes the provider's models (a built-in provider keeps its own).
entries.userImpact: An operation failed or was rejected
entries.releaseNote: A Node extension that registers or unregisters a provider through `ctx.modelRegistry` (or `pi.registerProvider`/`unregisterProvider`) sees the write on the next line, as Pi does: `find`, `getAll`, `getAvailable`, `hasConfiguredAuth`, `getProviderAuthStatus` and `isUsingOAuth` read the registry the registration left, and an unregistration removes the provider's models (a built-in provider keeps its own). The runtime keeps its own writes over the host's registry snapshot until the host answers the call, so a publication that predates the write cannot undo it.

entries.releaseNote: `ctx.abort()` aborts the run's `ctx.signal`, and the signal a tool receives, before it returns in a Node extension, as Pi's `agent.abort()` does. The host sends the run's `run_signal` frame ahead of the reply to the `abort` call, so the Go, Python and Rust SDKs read the signal aborted as soon as `abort()` returns instead of when a watcher's frame happens to win the race.

The dialog resolves with the client's JSON as Pi's does: a Node, Go, Python or Rust extension sees a number, `null`, an object or an array from `select`, `input` and `editor`, and the client's `confirmed` from `confirm`; `cancelled` is read by JavaScript truthiness.

entries.title: Two parallel `edit` calls through two names of one existing file (a hard link, or a case alias on a…
entries.symptom: Two parallel `edit` calls through two names of one existing file (a hard link, or a case alias on a case-insensitive filesystem such as the macOS default) no longer lose one of the edits.
entries.rootCause: both edits of two parallel `edit` calls through two names of one file read the same original text and each writes the whole file, so the later write silently drops the earlier edit while both calls report success.
entries.removeWhen: Pi orders hard-link aliases (and, on a case-insensitive filesystem where its `realpath` keeps case, case aliases) by file identity, or an owner decision reverses this one; then the identity check, its marker, the allowance test and this record go.
entries.releaseNote: Two parallel `edit` calls through two names of one existing file (a hard link, or a case alias on a case-insensitive filesystem such as the macOS default) no longer lose one of the edits. The built-in file mutation queue made them run at once, so both read the original text and the later write dropped the earlier edit while both calls reported success; it now orders them in call order. Pi does not order hard-link aliases (D190).

entries.releaseNote: A YAML date used as a mapping key is named with the time zone names of Node 24.22 and later, the Node Pi runs on (tz 2026e). Morocco and Western Sahara print "Western European Standard Time" and "Western European Summer Time" instead of "GMT+00:00" and "GMT+01:00" (Node 24.22.1 does so from 2026-09-20 01:00 UTC, when Morocco returned to permanent UTC); `EST5EDT`, `CST6CDT`, `MST7MDT` and `PST8PDT` print their offset (`GMT-05:00`) instead of the names of New York, Chicago, Denver and Los Angeles; and the switches between standard and daylight names of Alberta, Manitoba, the Northwest Territories, Colombia (1992) and Iran (1979) follow tz 2026e. Node 22.19 and 24.19 print other names for these zones.

entries.title: CI: `TestNodeCellAddedMembersStayWithinTheirOwnState` no longer fails under load
entries.symptom: CI: `TestNodeCellAddedMembersStayWithinTheirOwnState` no longer fails under load.
entries.userImpact: An operation failed or was rejected
entries.releaseNote: CI: `TestNodeCellAddedMembersStayWithinTheirOwnState` no longer fails under load. It compared the RSS of a one-member Node cell with the RSS of a five-member cell against 6 MiB per added member; one member's RSS read 131.8 to 152.2 MiB (6.4 to 27.5 MiB below its own peak) in 19 runs, so the figure ranged 0.8 to 7.2 MiB and failed once. The probe now reads the retained V8 heap plus external memory right after the forced collection, which gives 0.20 to 0.25 MiB per added member in every run, and the budget is 2 MiB.

entries.title: CI: a Node extension no longer holds a request the host sends it behind the highlight.js language load
entries.symptom: CI: a Node extension no longer holds a request the host sends it behind the highlight.js language load.
entries.releaseNote: CI: a Node extension no longer holds a request the host sends it behind the highlight.js language load. In TUI mode the runtime loads Pi's complete grammar set after the startup events, and `lib/index.js` evaluates its ~190 grammars in one synchronous pass on the thread that serves requests: 125 ms on an idle machine and more than the five-second renderer inactivity lease (D56) on a starved one, so a Markdown transform, render or mouse event sent meanwhile was abandoned while the extension was healthy and the proxy returned its input (`got ""` in `TestMarkdownContextsAcrossSDKs/subprocess-node-packed`). Each grammar module is now required on its own event-loop turn before that pass, which only registers them as in Pi.

entries.symptom: CI: a Node extension no longer holds the first request the host sends it behind its bytecode-cache flush.
entries.releaseNote: CI: a Node extension no longer holds the first request the host sends it behind its bytecode-cache flush. The runtime flushed Node's compile cache when it processed the host's ready message, on the thread that serves requests; the flush serializes every compiled module and took 4.6 s on a starved machine, so a Markdown transform sent right after registration passed the five-second renderer inactivity lease (D56) while the extension was healthy and the proxy returned its input (`got ""` in `TestMarkdownContextsAcrossSDKs/subprocess-node-packed`). The flush now runs when the factory has loaded, before the member registers.

entries.title: CI: `TestTerminalProgramGetsDefaultSignalsWhenTheDaemonStartedIgnoringThem` no longer fails every run under…
entries.symptom: CI: `TestTerminalProgramGetsDefaultSignalsWhenTheDaemonStartedIgnoringThem` no longer fails every run under `make test-fast`.

entries.releaseNote: CI: `TestTerminalProgramGetsDefaultSignalsWhenTheDaemonStartedIgnoringThem` no longer fails every run under `make test-fast`. It required every ignored-signal bit of the terminal's program to be clear, but Pi's `pty.rs` (and PiG's daemon, which mirrors it) resets signals 1 through 31 only, and GNU make 4.4.1 starts its recipes with signals 32 and 33 ignored, so the program ended with `SigIgn` 0x80000000 under both daemons. The test asserts signals 1 through 31, the daemon's contract.

entries.title: URL parsing follows Node 24.22 and later
entries.symptom: URL parsing follows Node 24.22 and later.
entries.releaseNote: URL parsing follows Node 24.22 and later. Pi runs on that Node, whose URL parser only lowercases an ASCII host: `https://xn--.example` and `ftp:xn--mailto:` are valid, `file://xn--a.b/x` is a UNC path on Windows, and a provider or Radius base such as `file:///C:ab/c` or `file:///u:p@[::1]:9000` no longer keeps its first path segment as a drive letter when a path is resolved against it.

entries.title: A packed Go, Python or Rust cell no longer hangs when a later member's factory calls the host before an…

entries.releaseNote: A packed Go, Python or Rust cell no longer hangs when a later member's factory calls the host before an earlier member's factory has run. The generated runner started every member on a thread of its own and let them race for the factory turn; the host accepts the members in order and serves a connection only after the members before it, so a later member whose factory subscribed to the event bus held the turn and waited for a host that waited for the earlier member. The runner now starts each member's factory in the cell's order.

entries.title: `pi.events.emit` in a Go, Rust or Python factory behaves as Pi's does: the first factory-time bus call…
entries.symptom: The emit was queued until after ready, and its failure only reached stderr.
entries.releaseNote: `pi.events.emit` in a Go, Rust or Python factory behaves as Pi's does: the first factory-time bus call connects to the host (as `parseFrontmatter` does) and `Run` reuses the connection; a listener the factory subscribes is registered with the host at once and answers the host's dispatches on that connection while the factory waits for a host call, so it hears another extension's emit made while the factory runs, a nested reply to the factory's own emit included, as Pi's shared emitter delivers it; the call returns once the host has delivered the emit to every listener, in registration order (the extensions loaded before this one, then this one's own), and each has finished; a listener that throws or panics is written to stderr as `Event handler error (channel):` and reaches neither the emitter nor the next listener; an `error` emit that nobody hears fails with the emitted error. Before, the emit was queued until after ready, and its failure only reached stderr. A factory with no host (no `PIG_EXT_SOCKET`) gets an error from its first bus call. Go gains `sdk.ServeFactory(conn, factory)` for a fused binary, which gives the factory the pipe as its connection.

entries.title: An edit or write call of a parallel batch registers in the file mutation queue after the extension tools…
entries.symptom: The built-in call registered in the dispatcher's loop, a process hop before the extension's registration arrived, so `[extension tool, write]` applied the write first.
entries.releaseNote: An edit or write call of a parallel batch registers in the file mutation queue after the extension tools before it in the batch took the queue, as Pi does: Pi registers a call in the queue when it calls `withFileMutationQueue` and runs each call's first statements in call order. Before, the built-in call registered in the dispatcher's loop, a process hop before the extension's registration arrived, so `[extension tool, write]` applied the write first. The Go, Python, Rust and Node SDKs, isolated, packed and fused, now agree. A native tool that waits on something other than a host call before it takes the queue still registers first, and a write behind a native tool that makes no host call waits for the tool; both are recorded in the parity row.

entries.title: An extension that reads `ctx.model`, `pi.getSettings()`, `pi.getSessionName()`, `pi.getThinkingLevel()` or…
entries.symptom: An extension that reads `ctx.model`, `pi.getSettings()`, `pi.getSessionName()`, `pi.getThinkingLevel()` or its footer's git branch and provider count from a timer, thread or goroutine between requests now sees a change the host makes itself.
entries.releaseNote: An extension that reads `ctx.model`, `pi.getSettings()`, `pi.getSessionName()`, `pi.getThinkingLevel()` or its footer's git branch and provider count from a timer, thread or goroutine between requests now sees a change the host makes itself. A model switch (Ctrl+P, `/model`, cycling, RPC `set_model`), a settings edit, `/name` or RPC `set_session_name`, a resumed session, a branch checkout and a login updated the host but reached an extension only at its next request, so a background reader held the old value; Pi reads the live session. The host now pushes the new state to every connected extension when it changes, off the UI loop, and sends nothing to an extension that already holds it.

The handler now edits the options through the `BeforeAgentStartEvent` the context shares, and a read after an edit asks the host to render the edited options.

entries.title: Starting a second Piglet Binary instance no longer fails on Windows while the first is running
entries.symptom: Starting a second Piglet Binary instance no longer fails on Windows while the first is running.
entries.userImpact: An operation failed or was rejected
entries.releaseNote: Starting a second Piglet Binary instance no longer fails on Windows while the first is running. Extraction left the embedded Go, Rust and Python cell binaries rewritten at every start, and Windows refuses to replace the executable of a running process (`Access is denied`); a cell binary that already holds the embedded bytes is now left in place, and only a different one is replaced, with a retry on a transient lock.

entries.title: RPC mode writes one `setWidget` request per `ctx.ui.setWidget` call from the Go, Python and Rust SDKs, in…

entries.releaseNote: RPC mode writes one `setWidget` request per `ctx.ui.setWidget` call from the Go, Python and Rust SDKs, in call order and before the command's response, as Pi does. A string list with no options went out as an unanswered frame that the host applied on a lane of its own: the last list a command set could be written after the command's response or after a later `notify`, a repeat of the same list was dropped, and a list set after a clear stayed cleared on the client. In RPC mode the SDKs now send the list as the host call every other widget shape uses.

entries.releaseNote: The interactive mode no longer rewrites every provider request's system prompt into one head. It set the agent's system prompt for every run and again after every tool change and reload, so a mid-session change to the prompt or the active tools reached the model as a rewritten head with the transcript's system patch messages dropped. entries.releaseNote: Interactive mode now routes a message an extension sends with `sendMessage` while a run streams as Pi does. A message with no `deliverAs` steers: the run delivers it after the current tool batch, before the next model call, where it used to wait until the run would stop. A message with `triggerTurn: false` is held until the turn's tool results are complete and appended without a model call, where it used to be queued as a follow-up that cost the run another model call. `sendMessage` no longer rejects an empty `customType` or an unknown `deliverAs` (Pi accepts the first and steers the second).

entries.title: fix(extensions): run a tick call after the tool_execution_end of the tool call that queued its callback…

entries.rootCause: A timer or immediate callback a Node tool queued while a sibling tool still awaits runs, in Pi, right after the first tool's tool_execution_end. The runtime is another process: it writes the callback's host call a few hundred microseconds after the tool's answer, and the host passed the tick boundary of that tool in about the same time. A call that arrived after the boundary was held for the next tool_execution_end of any tool, so scenario 69 (rpc-sibling-tool-timer-call-order) wrote the immediate and timeout0 notifications behind the sibling's own notification in 8 of 20 single-pair runs on ordering/d5-timer-calls alone and 4 of 20 on the train.

entries.rootCause: A timer or immediate callback a Node tool queued while a sibling tool still awaits runs, in Pi, right after the first tool's tool_execution_end. The runtime is another process: it writes the callback's host call a few hundred microseconds after the tool's answer, and the host passed the tick boundary of that tool in about the same time. A call that arrived after the boundary was held for the next tool_execution_end of any tool, so scenario 69 (rpc-sibling-tool-timer-call-order) wrote the immediate and timeout0 notifications behind the sibling's own notification in 8 of 20 single-pair runs on ordering/d5-timer-calls alone and 4 of 20 on the train.
entries.releaseNote: A notification, status or message that an extension queued with `setImmediate` or `setTimeout` from a tool that returned while a sibling tool in the same batch still awaited reached an RPC client behind the sibling's own output in up to two runs in five, where Pi writes it right after the first tool's `tool_execution_end`. The Node runtime is another process: it wrote the callback's host call a few hundred microseconds after the tool's answer, and the host passed that tool's `tool_execution_end` in about the same time, so a call that arrived after it waited for the next `tool_execution_end` of any tool. The call now says which tool call queued its callback (`origin_tool_call_id`). The host runs it behind that call's `tool_execution_end` when it arrives before the event, and at once when it arrives after, where the runtime says a sibling tool still runs and the loop turns.

entries.rootCause: Differences found: every message used Go's %q where Pi interpolates the name between plain double quotes (constrained-sampling.ts:136-150,188,226,259,267), so a tool named 'we"ird' got backslashes; isStructuredSchema tested properties/items with != nil although JS tests !== undefined (an explicit null counts) and searched a type array through toStringSlice, which gave up when any element was not a string where Array.includes does not. entries.title: `/export` to a directory that cannot be created on a read-only file system (such as macOS's root) reports…
entries.symptom: `/export` to a directory that cannot be created on a read-only file system (such as macOS's root) reports `ENOENT: no such file or directory, mkdir ...` as Pi does, not `EROFS`.
entries.rootCause: node_file.cc MKDirpSync returns EACCES, ENOSPC, ENOTDIR, EPERM and ENOENT from mkdir as they are; for any other error it stats the directory and reports that error. A directory missing from macOS's read-only root is therefore ENOENT in Node (and Pi's /export), where MkdirAll said EROFS. TestExportSessionToJsonlFailuresAreNodes now takes the expected message from Node's mkdirSync on the running OS (EACCES on Linux, ENOENT on macOS).

entries.title: Tool-argument validation compares JSON values as JSON Schema does: a number is never equal to a string
entries.symptom: Tool-argument validation compares JSON values as JSON Schema does: a number is never equal to a string.
entries.rootCause: The vendored santhosh-tekuri equals() parsed the right-hand side of a numeric left-hand side with big.Rat.SetString, which accepts "1.5", "0x10", "1e3" and "1/2". A schema {"const":"1"} accepted the number 1 (Pi's typebox rejects it), {"const":{"x":"1"}} accepted {"x":1}, and uniqueItems rejected ["1", 1] or ["0x10", 16] (Pi accepts them) when the string came first.
entries.releaseNote: Tool-argument validation compares JSON values as JSON Schema does: a number is never equal to a string. `const`, `enum` and `uniqueItems` no longer treat `1`, `1.5`, `16` or `0.5` as equal to `"1"`, `"1.5"`, `"0x10"` or `"1/2"` (the schema library parsed the string as a number), matching Pi's validator.

Pig took os.Getwd's $PWD, so from a symlinked directory 'pig list' printed a project package's path through the link and '--session empty.jsonl' recorded the link as the session cwd. New binary tests run pig through a symlink with PWD=link. Package tests that set up sources from t.TempDir() and then ran the CLI there now start from the physical temp dir, the directory Pi's process.cwd() would report (they mixed /var and /private/var on macOS).

entries.title: A session message with a member of another JSON type than Pi writes is now kept, as Pi keeps it
entries.symptom: PiG dropped the message from the session context, the projection and RPC `get_messages`.
entries.rootCause: parseSessionEntryLine keeps any JSON.parse value as an entry's message (session-manager.ts:617-623), and buildSessionContext and the projection push it as is, so Pi keeps a message that is a number, a string or an array in its context, projection and get_messages. PiG dropped it. decodeLax now decodes such a message as a custom message without members that keeps its text, and SourceJSON writes that text. Having no role, it reaches no provider, as Pi's convertToLlm default case returns undefined (messages.ts:189-192). A null message stays undecodable: Pi's context build throws reading its role (getSessionContextSettings).
entries.releaseNote: A session message with a member of another JSON type than Pi writes is now kept, as Pi keeps it. Examples are a string `timestamp`, numeric `content`, a text block whose `text` is a number, a usage count written as a string, `isError: "no"`, a numeric or missing `role`, and a message that is a number, a string or an array rather than an object. Before, PiG dropped the message from the session context, the projection and RPC `get_messages`. The message is written exactly as it was read. PiG reads a wrong-typed member as absent. An object or array member keeps the parts that have the right types. A content block with an unknown or wrong-typed `type` is left out of the provider request, as Pi's provider conversions skip it.

entries.title: A Session delivers each event to its listeners the way Pi's `AgentSession` does
entries.symptom: Every delivery used the list as it was when the delivery began.
entries.rootCause: EmitMessage/EmitError/EmitClose now visit the next entry registered after the last one run. New tests: the live-set emit, the closed-end drop and placement hook of InMemoryTransport, the redirect mix-up page and context cause of OAuthCallbackServer, SetProtocolVersion's header, McpAbortError's defaults. 71 mutants recorded; equivalents listed in evidence.
entries.releaseNote: A Session delivers each event to its listeners the way Pi's `AgentSession` does. A listener that unsubscribes itself or another listener during delivery changes which listeners that delivery still reaches, and a listener subscribed during delivery receives the same event. Before, every delivery used the list as it was when the delivery began.

entries.symptom: Every id in the request was rewritten, including the model's own.
entries.rootCause: openai-completions.ts convertMessages gives normalizeToolCallId to transformMessages, which applies it to a tool call of another model (transform-messages.ts:136-139) and maps its result to the new id. PiG instead rewrote every id in the converted request messages, so a same-model call with a '|' id or, on provider openai, an id over 40 characters was changed where Pi sends it as is. convertTranscript now passes the normalizer to transformMessages and the post-pass is gone.
entries.releaseNote: OpenAI-compatible chat completions requests keep the tool-call ids of the same model's earlier calls as they were sent. As in Pi, only a tool call of another model is normalized: a `|`-separated id is shortened, and on the `openai` provider an id over 40 characters is truncated. Before, every id in the request was rewritten, including the model's own.

entries.title: Markdown list items lex their text line by line like Pi: an HTML block starts at any item line, and an item…
entries.symptom: Markdown list items lex their text line by line like Pi: an HTML block starts at any item line, and an item line indented four or more spaces past the content joins the text before it (so a heading, quote, rule, fence, table or bullet there stays text) and leaves an empty row before the text that follows.
entries.rootCause: Pi lexes a list item's text with top false: no paragraph rule, so an HTML block (including a custom tag, comment or pre) starts at any item line indented up to three spaces, and a line indented four or more past the item's content is indented code that blockTokens joins to the text before it with four spaces removed, plus a newline that leaves an empty row before the text that follows. entries.title: A streaming run no longer hangs, rarely and mostly under load, when a response turn resumes just as the drain…
entries.symptom: A streaming run no longer hangs, rarely and mostly under load, when a response turn resumes just as the drain that granted it ends: a pausing coroutine put back a drain flag the ending drain had already cleared, which left every goroutine asleep with a reaction still queued.
entries.rootCause: settle saved the executor's draining flag at entry and wrote it back when the body went on to pause. For a body that a serving goroutine claimed (needsDriver) the flag belongs to the drain that granted it, live on another goroutine and about to end; when that end landed in settle's unlocked reaction window, the write-back set draining again with no loop on any stack. serve and startDrainLocked then refused to drain, and the queued reactions never ran (a lost wakeup seen as a hang of TestGoogleVertexProviderStreamMatchesPi under -race).
entries.releaseNote: A streaming run no longer hangs, rarely and mostly under load, when a response turn resumes just as the drain that granted it ends: a pausing coroutine put back a drain flag the ending drain had already cleared, which left every goroutine asleep with a reaction still queued.

entries.title: On arm64, `tool_search` and `searchTools()` scores use the same natural logarithm as Pi running on Node for…
entries.symptom: The logarithm in the BM25 weights differed from Node's in the last bit for about 1 in 500 arguments, which could change scores and break ties in a different order.
entries.rootCause: Math.log is V8's fdlibm port in C++, not JavaScript arithmetic. Node's arm64 builds compile it with clang, whose default -ffp-contract=on fuses a product into the addition or subtraction of the same C expression (never across statements). Node 24.19 on darwin-arm64 matches that variant bit for bit over TestLogMatchesNode's 360022 inputs.
entries.releaseNote: On arm64, `tool_search` and `searchTools()` scores use the same natural logarithm as Pi running on Node for arm64, whose V8 math library fuses each multiply-add in one step. Before, the logarithm in the BM25 weights differed from Node's in the last bit for about 1 in 500 arguments, which could change scores and break ties in a different order.

entries.title: An extension that writes a large amount to stderr no longer grows its diagnostic log without limit
entries.symptom: An extension that writes a large amount to stderr no longer grows its diagnostic log without limit.
entries.rootCause: Host wire (go-vs-rust-harness #10): an outbound frame is encoded into a pooled buffer holding the length prefix and written with one socket write; Send allocates nothing in steady state (was 1 object, 20 us -> 8.6 us). Every extension process's stderr goes through a log that keeps the first 1 MiB and the last 64 KiB and counts the bytes it dropped, so a flood neither blocks the pipe nor fills the disk.
entries.releaseNote: An extension that writes a large amount to stderr no longer grows its diagnostic log without limit. The log keeps the first 1 MiB and the last 64 KiB of the output and says how many bytes it dropped, so a startup failure and a crash line both survive a flood.

entries.title: RPC mode no longer hangs when a Node extension command calls `pi.sendMessage(..., { triggerTurn: true })`…
entries.symptom: RPC mode no longer hangs when a Node extension command calls `pi.sendMessage(..., { triggerTurn: true })` while a `before_agent_start` handler is subscribed: the handler runs inside the call, as in Pi, and the run starts after the command's response.
entries.rootCause: TestRPCCommandTurnStartOrderMatchesPi/async-followup hung (agent_settled timed out). An earlier change made a triggering pi.sendMessage a synchronous bridge call, so before_agent_start starts nested in that call's wait; its synchronous prefix ran (setStatus was written), but the handler's suspension was never reported, because the rest of it waits on the call's own answer. The host waited for the suspension, the runtime for the answer: a deadlock. A request started nested in a synchronous call now reports "blocked" (host_call) once its synchronous prefix returns, unless its handler reported the suspension already (session_info_changed, thinking_level_select).
entries.releaseNote: RPC mode no longer hangs when a Node extension command calls `pi.sendMessage(..., { triggerTurn: true })` while a `before_agent_start` handler is subscribed: the handler runs inside the call, as in Pi, and the run starts after the command's response.

entries.title: `find` and `grep` trim like JavaScript: `FindTool` trimmed each fd output line with `strings.TrimSpace` where…
entries.symptom: `find` and `grep` trim like JavaScript: `FindTool` trimmed each fd output line with `strings.TrimSpace` where find.ts:270 uses `String.prototype.trim`, so a file whose name ends with U+FEFF lost nothing in Pi but a name ending in U+0085 lost it in PiG (and the reverse).
entries.rootCause: JSON.parse keeps a member of any type, so Pi keeps a session message whose member has another type than Pi writes, in its entries, branch, context, projection and RPC get_messages (session-manager.ts parseSessionEntryLine, buildSessionContext). PiG's AgentMessage decode failed on such a member and dropped the message from the context, the projection and get_messages: a string timestamp, numeric content, a text block with a numeric text, a usage count written "1", isError "no", a numeric or missing role, and so on.
entries.releaseNote: `find` and `grep` trim like JavaScript: `FindTool` trimmed each fd output line with `strings.TrimSpace` where find.ts:270 uses `String.prototype.trim`, so a file whose name ends with U+FEFF lost nothing in Pi but a name ending in U+0085 lost it in PiG (and the reverse). `find`'s lines and stderr message and `grep`'s stderr message and blank-line check now use `jsstring.Trim` (find.ts:252,270; grep.ts:220,252). New live-Pi oracle `TestFindTrimsOutputLinesLikeJavaScript` (`internal/codingagent/tools/find_trim_names_oracle_test.go`: names beginning or ending with U+FEFF, U+0085, U+00A0 or a space, and names that are only U+FEFF or U+0085); red before the fix (3 of 7 directories), green after; `./internal/codingagent/tools -race` green. The stderr and ripgrep blank-line trims are not reachable by the oracle (they need fd or rg to fail or emit a blank JSON line) and are changed for the same rule only.

entries.title: A resumed session no longer holds its whole file in memory
entries.symptom: A resumed session no longer holds its whole file in memory.
entries.rootCause: The range is now 225-285 MB.
entries.releaseNote: A resumed session no longer holds its whole file in memory. PiG keeps a small index of every entry and decodes only what the active context needs (the latest compaction's kept messages and everything after them); older entries are read back from the session file when a command such as `/tree`, `/fork` or export needs them. On a real 314 MB session, an interactive resume measured 150-190 MB after loading and 225-285 MB after opening `/tree` (two profiling runs on macOS), where PiG 0.4.1 took 1.2-1.3 GB and Pi 1.1.0 about 700 MB. History outside the active context is not kept decoded, so a long-open session file does not accumulate it in memory.

entries.title: Repairing a partial tool-call arguments text follows partial-json's `obj["__proto__"] = value`: a…
entries.symptom: Repairing a partial tool-call arguments text follows partial-json's `obj["__proto__"] = value`: a `"__proto__": null` member leaves the object without a prototype, so a later `"__proto__"` member is an ordinary member, as in Pi (it was dropped).
entries.rootCause: partial-json builds objects with obj[key] = value. A "__proto__" member runs Object.prototype's setter: null makes the prototype null, an object or array replaces it, any other value is ignored, and none creates a property. Once the prototype is null there is no setter, so a later "__proto__" member is an ordinary member. parseMembers dropped every "__proto__" member.

entries.title: A Node extension no longer keeps reading an entry the host refused
entries.symptom: A Node extension no longer keeps reading an entry the host refused.
entries.rootCause: Fixes #264
entries.releaseNote: A Node extension no longer keeps reading an entry the host refused. When the host answers `pi.appendEntry` (or `ctx.sessionManager.appendCustomEntry`) with an error, `getEntries()`, `getBranch()`, `getLeafId()`, `getEntry()` and the other session reads stop showing that entry, also after later calls the host synchronizes; before, the entry stayed in the extension's session reads although the host's log never held it. Only the refused entry is taken back: appends still in flight stay, and an entry the host appended is read with the parent the host linked it to, where the extension could show the refused entry or an older leaf instead. A call that was cancelled or lost with its connection has no answer, so its entry stays until the host's log settles it.

entries.title: A long session no longer holds each tool result twice
entries.symptom: A long session no longer holds each tool result twice.
entries.rootCause: Pi's session holds the message object the agent appended (session-manager.ts appendMessage pushes it into fileEntries), so a tool result is in memory once. appendMessageEntry kept the appended message only when its record decoded DeepEqual to it, and a tool result never does: its record decodes Details to their JSON (orderedjson.Value), while the tool gave a typed value (ReadDetails, BashDetails, EditToolDetails, ...) or an extension a map. So every tool result was held twice, as the agent's message and as the record's decode, text included.
entries.releaseNote: A long session no longer holds each tool result twice. The session now keeps the tool result the agent produced instead of a second copy decoded from its record, and a truncated `read`, `ls`, `find`, `grep` or `bash` result keeps its kept output once instead of again in its truncation details. In a 75-prompt session of file reads (about 4.2M tokens of context), memory at the end drops from about 245 MB to about 170 MB.

Concurrent replacements raced in Runner.BindCommandActions and hung at stdin end about one run in two. - A fork or clone requested while an earlier replacement is pending reads its entry from the Session that was current when it…

entries.title: `PIG_PROFILE=metrics` reports the exact cumulative allocation counts
entries.symptom: This fix it missed allocations still held in the runtime's per-processor caches, so a record could be as much as half a megabyte low, depending on whether a garbage collection happened to run shortly before exit.
entries.rootCause: PIG_PROFILE=metrics read /gc/heap/allocs through runtime/metrics, which does not flush the per-P mcaches. A span still cached keeps its allocations out of the counter until a refill or a collection, so the record undercounted by up to ~500 KB depending on whether a GC happened to run shortly before exit. That made process.rpc_startup.bytes bimodal: 2.79 MB on a quiet host and 3.38 MB under load. The high value is the real one. CollectMetrics now flushes with ReadMemStats before it reads the counters (TestCollectMetricsCountsAllocations InCachedSpans; it was red 4/5 before).
entries.releaseNote: `PIG_PROFILE=metrics` reports the exact cumulative allocation counts. Before this fix it missed allocations still held in the runtime's per-processor caches, so a record could be as much as half a megabyte low, depending on whether a garbage collection happened to run shortly before exit.

entries.title: An OpenAI Chat Completions chunk with a member of an unexpected type (a number for `delta.content`…
entries.symptom: An OpenAI Chat Completions chunk with a member of an unexpected type (a number for `delta.content`, `delta.tool_calls` or `function.arguments`, a non-object `choices` or `delta`, a non-string `delta.role` or tool call `type`, a falsy `custom`, a tool call element that is not an object) is read as Pi's JavaScript reads it: the member is ignored, tool-call arguments append their string form, a `tool_calls` string makes one empty tool call per character, any other `tool_calls` value that is not an array ends the turn with `choice.delta.tool_calls is not iterable`, non-empty array content (or an object with a positive `length`) appends its string form, a truthy `finish_reason` that is not a string ends the turn with `Provider finish_reason: <its string form>`, a usage that is not an object resets the counts to 0, a falsy count or a details member that is not an object reads as 0, and a prompt count that is not a number counts as its Number() when that is an integer.
entries.rootCause: Pi reads `event.message.id` and `event.message.usage.input_tokens` (anthropic-messages.ts:666, :679), `event.content_block.type` (:690), `event.delta.type` (:737) and `event.delta.stop_reason` (:818) without a guard, so a null or absent member throws `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'x')` (or `of undefined`) and the turn ends with that error; the response id and model are recorded before the usage read throws. PiG's typed decode read each as an empty value and streamed on.
entries.userImpact: An operation failed or was rejected
entries.releaseNote: An OpenAI Chat Completions chunk with a member of an unexpected type (a number for `delta.content`, `delta.tool_calls` or `function.arguments`, a non-object `choices` or `delta`, a non-string `delta.role` or tool call `type`, a falsy `custom`, a tool call element that is not an object) is read as Pi's JavaScript reads it: the member is ignored, tool-call arguments append their string form, a `tool_calls` string makes one empty tool call per character, any other `tool_calls` value that is not an array ends the turn with `choice.delta.tool_calls is not iterable`, non-empty array content (or an object with a positive `length`) appends its string form, a truthy `finish_reason` that is not a string ends the turn with `Provider finish_reason: <its string form>`, a usage that is not an object resets the counts to 0, a falsy count or a details member that is not an object reads as 0, and a prompt count that is not a number counts as its Number() when that is an integer. An Anthropic `content_block_delta` with a missing or non-numeric index matches no block and its text, thinking, partial-JSON and signature members append their string form. An Anthropic `message_start`, `content_block_start` or `message_delta` is read the same way: a usage, delta or content block that is not an object reads as empty, a falsy `message_start` count is 0, a block's text, thinking or signature that is not a string starts with its string form, a model that is not a string becomes the response model's string form, and a truthy `stop_reason` that is not a string ends the turn with `Unhandled stop reason: <its string form>`. A null or missing message, message usage, content block or delta ends the turn with Pi's `Cannot read properties of null` (or `undefined`) error instead of streaming on. Other mistyped members still end the turn with the decode error.

entries.rootCause: redactJsonValue is JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value)); RedactBugReportJSON kept the number text it decoded with UseNumber, so -0, 1e21 and a 30-digit integer reached the report as -0, 1e21 and the digits where Pi writes 0, 1e+21 and 1.+29. TestBugReportRedactionMatchesPi compares 1500 URLs (schemes, nested schemes, userinfo, IPv6 and IDN hosts, dot segments, percent-encoding, repeated and mixed-case query keys, fragments, non-URLs) and 800 JSON values (sensitive keys in snake, kebab and camel case, nested containers, null members) with Pi's redactUrl and redactJsonValue; the URLs all matched, the numbers did not (red first). Numbers are now canonicalised through jsonstringify.
entries.userImpact: An operation failed or was rejected
entries.releaseNote: A JSON syntax error reports what V8's `JSON.parse` reports in two cases it got wrong: a number or string where a `true`, `false` or `null` literal breaks off (`t1`, `fals"`) is "Unexpected number" or "Unexpected string in JSON at position N", and a backslash followed by a character above U+00FF in a string is "Unexpected token" rather than "Bad escaped character".

entries.title: Two PiG versions that share a config root (two installed versions, or PiG beside a Piglet Binary) no longer…
entries.symptom: Two PiG versions that share a config root (two installed versions, or PiG beside a Piglet Binary) no longer restage each other's extension SDKs at every start or delete each other's extension builds.
entries.rootCause: Two PiG builds that share a config root (two installed versions, or stock PiG beside a Piglet Binary) staged into the same state/pigsdk/sdk, sdk-py and sdk-rs, so every switch restaged all three and pruned every extension build made against the other build's SDK, and a Python extension of one build could import the other build's SDK.
entries.releaseNote: Two PiG versions that share a config root (two installed versions, or PiG beside a Piglet Binary) no longer restage each other's extension SDKs at every start or delete each other's extension builds. Each version stages its SDKs into its own directory under `state/pigsdk`, named for the SDK's content hash, and reads only that directory, so a Python extension also always runs against its own version's SDK. After staging, PiG keeps the 4 most recently used SDK directories per language and drops only the extension builds whose SDK is gone. `pig reload --sdk-path` prints the running version's directory, and `pig diagnose` shows it.

The body is now walked untyped in Pi's order, so the id, usage and text read before a failing member stay on the result.
