entries.title: On Windows, PiG no longer searches `C:\etc\pig\piglets` or `C:\opt\pig\piglet.yaml` for a Piglet
entries.symptom: On Windows, PiG no longer searches `C:\etc\pig\piglets` or `C:\opt\pig\piglet.yaml` for a Piglet.
entries.rootCause: testenv.Start/Run/Output/CombinedOutput start a child in its own process group (Windows: kill-on-close Job Object), bound Wait with WaitDelay, stop the group SIGTERM then SIGKILL at cleanup, and fail the test when a descendant outlives an exited child. The lazy-startup test's logging shim guards against a real tool that re-execs the shim (PID sentinel) and starts the real tool without the shim directory on PATH. The D157 read-only-root test now expects no warning, and the --no-stdin help line no longer trips the strip leak gate.
entries.releaseNote: On Windows, PiG no longer searches `C:\etc\pig\piglets` or `C:\opt\pig\piglet.yaml` for a Piglet. A rooted path without a volume is drive-relative there, so any local user could plant a Piglet that every other user's `pig` loaded.

entries.title: A Durable Harness task that went to sleep for a short time, such as the 1 ms backoff before a generation…
entries.symptom: A Durable Harness task that went to sleep for a short time, such as the 1 ms backoff before a generation retry, could stay asleep for good on a busy machine, so a `Wait` on its submission never returned (a CI run of the `durable/harness` tests hung until the 10-minute timeout).
entries.releaseNote: A Durable Harness task that went to sleep for a short time, such as the 1 ms backoff before a generation retry, could stay asleep for good on a busy machine, so a `Wait` on its submission never returned (a CI run of the `durable/harness` tests hung until the 10-minute timeout). The Harness recomputes when to wake the process in a goroutine that can run milliseconds after the change, and it read the clock when that goroutine ran, not at the change, as Pi's microtask does. A sleep that had been ahead of a scheduling pass was then already due, so no timer was armed for it, and a host's `onWake` was told that work was active instead of the time to wake at; nothing ran the task again. The recomputation now reads the clock of the change that queued it, so the timer is armed (or the time is offered to `onWake`) and the task wakes.

entries.title: On Windows, the bash tool no longer risks waiting forever after a command exits while a process it started in…
entries.symptom: On Windows, the bash tool no longer risks waiting forever after a command exits while a process it started in the background still holds the output pipe.
entries.rootCause: The bash tool on Windows puts the shell in a job object. When the shell exits, `processGroupMayHoldOutput` asks Windows whether the job still has processes (`QueryInformationJobObject`, `JobObjectBasicAccountingInformation`). If the answer is zero, `childwait.waitIdle` waits for the output pipe to reach EOF with no further bound, because an empty job means no process can still hold the pipe.
entries.releaseNote: On Windows, the bash tool no longer risks waiting forever after a command exits while a process it started in the background still holds the output pipe. The check that asks Windows whether the command's job still has processes could read an empty answer when Go moved the goroutine stack during the call, and the tool then waited for the pipe to close. The buffers these job-object calls pass to Windows now stay in place.

entries.title: Selecting a model or cycling models with Ctrl+P no longer freezes the interactive mode when an extension's…
entries.symptom: Selecting a model or cycling models with Ctrl+P no longer freezes the interactive mode when an extension's `model_select` handler registers a tool.
entries.rootCause: Pi's shutdown ends with process.exit and does not await a pending model_select (interactive-mode.ts:4251-4291). PiG's notification Emit ran on the Session's background context, so Stop's backgroundTasks.Wait joined a slow or hung handler. /quit, Ctrl+D or a signal therefore tore the UI down but did not exit.
entries.releaseNote: Selecting a model or cycling models with Ctrl+P no longer freezes the interactive mode when an extension's `model_select` handler registers a tool. As in Pi, the mode no longer waits for the handlers, whether the change comes from Ctrl+P, the model selector or a typed `/model`. The new model applies at once, and keys typed while the handlers run reach the focused component: the model selector, which stays open until the change settles (Escape closes it at once), or the editor. A prompt submitted meanwhile starts at once on the new model. A second change applies its model at once, and its handlers run alongside the first change's. An extension dialog opened meanwhile closes the selector, so later keys reach the editor. Quitting while a handler still runs no longer waits for it, and a failed model switch shows the error's message, as Pi does.

entries.title: `--no-stdin` skips the startup read of piped stdin (Pi #10415)
entries.symptom: `pig --no-stdin -p "prompt"` with an open stdin pipe runs the prompt; Pi hangs. Pi parses `--no-stdin` as an unknown extension flag.
entries.rootCause: `pi -p hi < <(sleep 15)` never starts: `readPipedStdin` (`packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:80-97`) waits for `end` on a pipe whose writer stays open, and the same happens in PiG. An idle open pipe cannot be told from a slow producer, so a timeout would drop real input; an explicit opt-out is the only fix that cannot lose piped input. Callers that keep an input pipe open (agent harnesses, CI wrappers) pass the flag. Pi has no fix: Pi #10415 has an unmerged `--no-stdin` proposal and no PR. Pi #5571 discusses the same hang.

entries.symptom: memory use of a `grep` call follows the context size, not the file size. A custom `GrepOperations.ReadFile` still returns the whole text, but only the current file is kept. A custom `GrepOperations` without `ReadFile` streams the local file.
entries.rootCause: with `context: 2` over a directory of 100 MB logs, Pi holds each matched file several times over (read string, split array) and exhausts the heap (Pi #9276). Pi has no fix. The output is the same: the window splits lines as `getFileLines` does, keeps the first `GrepMaxLineLength + 1` code points of a line (the rest cannot reach the output), and still prints overlapping context blocks for nearby matches.

entries.title: A `read` result shown in the transcript no longer keeps the file text a second time as its structured content
entries.symptom: A `read` result shown in the transcript no longer keeps the file text a second time as its structured content.
entries.rootCause: A finished tool card keeps its result for its renderers, and its body renderer closure keeps it too, for as long as the transcript shows the card. entries.title: On Linux, clipboard reads accept every `DISPLAY` spelling Pi's `xcb_connect` accepts: white space or a sign…
entries.symptom: Previously these spellings failed, and image and text paste reported the clipboard as unavailable.
entries.rootCause: Pi opens the clipboard with xcb_connect (linux-platform-x11.c:185), whose parser reads the display and screen with C strtoul into an int (libxcb 1.15 xcb_util.c:176, :186): leading white space and a sign are accepted, a minus negates modulo 2^64, an overflow saturates, the int keeps the low 32 bits, and a network display's port is the low 16 bits of 6000 plus the number (:244). Pi then steps past screen_number screens (linux-platform-x11.c:188), so a negative screen selects the first. PiG used strconv.Atoi and rejected negative numbers and TCP displays above 59535, so DISPLAY=": 1", ":1.-1" or "host:65536+n" failed where Pi connects.
entries.userImpact: An operation failed or was rejected
entries.releaseNote: On Linux, clipboard reads accept every `DISPLAY` spelling Pi's `xcb_connect` accepts: white space or a sign before the display or screen number (`: 1`, `:+1`), a negative screen, which selects the first screen, and display numbers that wrap as libxcb's `strtoul` and 16-bit port do (`host:65536` reaches port 6000). Previously these spellings failed, and image and text paste reported the clipboard as unavailable.

entries.title: NO_PROXY entries and ports are trimmed with JavaScript's whitespace rules, as in Pi: an entry or port that…
entries.symptom: NO_PROXY entries and ports are trimmed with JavaScript's whitespace rules, as in Pi: an entry or port that starts with U+0085 is no longer stripped, and one that starts with U+FEFF is.
entries.rootCause: It went red on U+0085: Go's TrimSpace stripped a leading NEL from a NO_PROXY entry (parseNoProxyEntry, node-http-proxy.ts:42 entry.trim()) and from a port (Number.parseInt), where JavaScript does not, so a proxied target was excluded. parseNoProxyEntry uses jsstring.Trim then jsstring.ToLower in Pi's order, proxyPort jsstring.TrimStart (parseInt ignores trailing text), and the two NO_PROXY lowercase calls use jsstring.ToLower. The ToLower swaps on the whole NO_PROXY text and the target host are unobservable here (entries are lowercased again, and the URL parser already gave an ASCII host); they stay as Pi writes them. Trim vs TrimStart on the port is equivalent.
entries.releaseNote: NO_PROXY entries and ports are trimmed with JavaScript's whitespace rules, as in Pi: an entry or port that starts with U+0085 is no longer stripped, and one that starts with U+FEFF is.

entries.title: A Radius gateway config cached on an OAuth credential is sanitized as Pi does
entries.symptom: A Radius gateway config cached on an OAuth credential is sanitized as Pi does.
entries.rootCause: Pi reads the exact properties. baseUrl and models now come from the exact-key member map. - A gateway model was decoded through the same struct first, so "ID", "Name" or "contextwindow" after "id", "name", "contextWindow" replaced Pi's value (the model id changed). Every model is now decoded member by member by exact key (radiusGatewayModelMembers, formerly the lenient fallback only). - The fallback clamped a number member to int32: 3e9 became 2147483647 while 3000000000 decoded exactly; 1e400 (Infinity in Pi) became 0. jsNumberToInt keeps the integer part over the whole int range, with Infinity as the largest int. Mutants killed: struct-first decode, int32 clamp, no clamp, floor for trunc…
entries.releaseNote: A Radius gateway config cached on an OAuth credential is sanitized as Pi does. A model whose `contextWindow` or `maxTokens` is `null` is dropped (it was kept). A model with a fractional or out-of-range window, a non-object cost tier, `headers` that are not a string map or another member Pig cannot represent is kept (it was dropped): a window keeps its integer part, clamped to the integer range, and any other such member is left at its zero value. `baseUrl`, `models` and each model member are read by their exact key, so a member such as `ID` or `contextwindow` no longer replaces `id` or `contextWindow`.

entries.title: A panic in a background goroutine of an interactive session no longer ends PiG with only a stderr dump
entries.symptom: A panic in a background goroutine of an interactive session no longer ends PiG with only a stderr dump.
entries.rootCause: Every other exit the user did not ask for now leaves a trace (D102, additive): an exit.log line in the agent directory for SIGHUP, SIGTERM, an external SIGINT, a closed terminal or input, an extension's shutdown() and a failed run; a crash record for a panic or fatal error in any goroutine (through a per-session crash-output marker the next start reconciles); and `pig diagnose` lists the recent unexpected exits. The background cache warm recovers a panic and reschedules as Pi's does, the emergency terminal exit stops extension processes, and a reconciled crash keeps its real time.
entries.releaseNote: A panic in a background goroutine of an interactive session no longer ends PiG with only a stderr dump. PiG restores the terminal, prints the error, records it in `crashes.json` and exits 1, as Pi does for an uncaught exception. Any other goroutine panic or runtime fatal error is copied to `<agent dir>/crash-output/` and becomes a crash record at the next start.

entries.title: In print and JSON mode, an extension whose `session_shutdown` handler throws after SIGTERM or SIGHUP now has…

entries.rootCause: SIGTERM during a tool: the signal's disposal awaits session_shutdown while the killed tool lets the run finish. Print mode's normal teardown then closed the runtime and retired the extension host under that in-flight request, so a throwing handler was reported as "Extension error (<path>): connection closed". Pi's finally awaits disposeRuntime, which does nothing once the signal handler has started it (print-mode.ts:42-48,162-167), and the process lives until the disposal settles (print-mode.ts:58-61), so Pi prints the handler's error. The teardown now joins the signal's disposal before it closes the runtime.

entries.title: `PIG_PROFILE=heap` and the `heap_live_bytes` of `PIG_PROFILE=metrics` count only memory PiG retains
entries.symptom: `PIG_PROFILE=heap` and the `heap_live_bytes` of `PIG_PROFILE=metrics` count only memory PiG retains.
entries.rootCause: PIG_PROFILE=heap and metrics heap_live_bytes ran one runtime.GC before measuring. The first cycle only moves sync.Pool contents to the victim cache, which keeps them reachable until the next cycle, so pooled buffers counted as live: at a 1M-token session the encoding/json encoder buffer of the last provider request showed as 4.5 MB at ai/openai.go json.Marshal (test/longsession measure, GODEBUG=memprofilerate=1: heap total 17.8 MB -> 13.2 MB with the fix).
entries.releaseNote: `PIG_PROFILE=heap` and the `heap_live_bytes` of `PIG_PROFILE=metrics` count only memory PiG retains. They now run two garbage collections before measuring. After the single collection used before, buffers that pools keep for reuse still counted as live, such as the JSON encoder buffer that holds the last provider request. At a 1M-token session that buffer is about 4.5 MB.

entries.title: Key matching follows Pi for more terminal inputs and key identifiers
entries.symptom: Key matching follows Pi for more terminal inputs and key identifiers.
entries.rootCause: - keys.ts's sequence patterns use \d+ (:597, :609, :620, :641, :697); Pig's Atoi accepted a sign (ESC[1;+5A, ESC[27;1;-1~ as up) and an arrow event with no digits (ESC[1;5:A). - parseInt yields a JavaScript number and the bitwise lock mask applies ToInt32, so ESC[1;4294967301A is ctrl+up in Pi; codepoints past 2^53 round (ESC[9007199254741039;5u is not ctrl+/). Pig refused or misread both. - parseKeyId (:788) ignores a part that names no modifier and lowercases with toLowerCase: meta+a matches a, hyper+up matches up, meta+f1 matches f1, ctrl+İ matches nothing. Pig matched none of the first three and read İ as i. Mutants killed: the inexact-modifier check, ToInt32 wrap, Unicode…
entries.releaseNote: Key matching follows Pi for more terminal inputs and key identifiers. Unmodified `enter` and `tab` no longer match an xterm modifyOtherKeys sequence. A sequence number with a sign (`ESC [ 1 ; +5 A`) or an event field with no digits (`ESC [ 1 ; 5 : A`) is no longer read as a key. Modifier and codepoint numbers are read as JavaScript numbers, so very large values wrap and round as in Pi. A key identifier part that names no modifier, such as `meta` in `meta+a`, is ignored as in Pi instead of making the identifier match nothing, and identifiers are lowercased as JavaScript's `toLowerCase` does.

entries.title: In print and JSON mode, a Node extension no longer runs a timer or other callback between a prompt's last…
entries.symptom: Pi-goal-x's `create_goal` could start a goal turn while the run was ending, print `Extension error (<runtime>): This extension ctx is stale ...` and leave the goal paused.
entries.rootCause: Pi's print and JSON modes await each prompt and go on in the same continuation: to the next prompt, or to disposeRuntime(), which emits session_shutdown and then invalidates the runner (print-mode.ts:131-166, agent-session-runtime.ts:404-410, agent-session.ts:1379-1392). A timer or immediate an extension queues in the prompt's last call therefore runs only after its ctx is stale. PiG's Node runtime answered over IPC and returned to its event loop first, so pi-goal-x's agent_settled continuation timer could start a goal turn during disposal, which failed with "This extension ctx is stale" and paused the goal.
entries.userImpact: An operation failed or was rejected
entries.releaseNote: In print and JSON mode, a Node extension no longer runs a timer or other callback between a prompt's last extension call (its command, a handled input or `agent_settled`) and `session_shutdown`, nor between `session_shutdown` and the runtime going stale. Pi runs those steps without an event-loop turn between them. Before, pi-goal-x's `create_goal` could start a goal turn while the run was ending, print `Extension error (<runtime>): This extension ctx is stale ...` and leave the goal paused.

entries.title: Model requests reuse their HTTP connection
entries.symptom: Every provider build used to create its own transport, so each request and tool round trip opened a new TCP (and TLS, and proxy CONNECT) connection and left an idle socket with its goroutines for two minutes.
entries.rootCause: Pi installs one process-wide dispatcher (core/http-dispatcher.ts configureHttpDispatcher), so requests reuse connections. PiG built a transport per provider: 20 requests opened 20 TCP connections and left idle sockets and goroutines. Cache the transport by TLS mode, idle timeout and proxy environment.
entries.releaseNote: Model requests reuse their HTTP connection. Every provider build used to create its own transport, so each request and tool round trip opened a new TCP (and TLS, and proxy CONNECT) connection and left an idle socket with its goroutines for two minutes. Providers now share one transport per TLS mode; a changed idle timeout or proxy environment replaces it, as Pi's configureHttpDispatcher replaces its single dispatcher.

entries.symptom: A resumed session draws its `!` and `!!` command blocks, as Pi does.

entries.title: When an extension in a shared Go, Rust or Python process crashes, the error for each stopped extension now…
entries.symptom: The message could only say "packed member connection closed".
entries.rootCause: A Go extension in a packed Go cell that exits mid-tool-call stops its healthy siblings in the same process. entries.title: A YAML parse error on a block scalar used as an implicit key (`name: x` followed by `|description: ...`)…
entries.symptom: A YAML parse error on a block scalar used as an implicit key (`name: x` followed by `|description: ...`) draws the carets of the `Implicit keys need to be on a single line` message as the yaml library does when the scalar's content holds a non-ASCII character: the range ends one UTF-16 unit per character after the key's offset, where it used to count bytes and print one caret or too many.
entries.rootCause: The library reports MULTILINE_IMPLICIT_KEY for a block scalar key at [offset, offset + source.length], where offset is the header and the source is the content that follows, so the range counts the content's UTF-16 units from the header. posOfToken added the content's byte length to the byte offset and converted that, so a multi-byte character in the content moved the end past the line and the message printed one caret, or too many ("a: 1\n|b: x\nÿ: 1" printed 1 caret, the library 5). pos now carries the length in units and prettify adds it to the converted start.
entries.userImpact: An operation failed or was rejected
entries.releaseNote: A YAML parse error on a block scalar used as an implicit key (`name: x` followed by `|description: ...`) draws the carets of the `Implicit keys need to be on a single line` message as the yaml library does when the scalar's content holds a non-ASCII character: the range ends one UTF-16 unit per character after the key's offset, where it used to count bytes and print one caret or too many.

entries.title: Starting `pig` no longer waits for the daily cleanup of the extension cache
entries.symptom: Starting `pig` no longer waits for the daily cleanup of the extension cache.
entries.rootCause: The prune loop checks for cancellation only before each entry. A busy failure that arrived after the cancellation counted as skipped, and the last entry's classification could be cut short with nothing to remove, so the collection returned success and the automatic collector wrote its marker for a run that did not finish. The collection now checks for cancellation before it reports success.
entries.userImpact: An operation failed or was rejected
entries.releaseNote: Starting `pig` no longer waits for the daily cleanup of the extension cache. The cleanup now runs in the background after the session is running, stops when `pig` exits, and skips entries that are in use or that the file system reports busy (such as NFS `.nfs*` files) instead of failing and repeating at every start. `pig extensions cache prune` reports the skipped entries, and `pig extensions cache stats` shows the last background failure.

entries.title: Session and crash timestamps are read like Date.parse of a JavaScript string: U+00A0 and U+FEFF between…
entries.symptom: Session and crash timestamps are read like Date.parse of a JavaScript string: U+00A0 and U+FEFF between tokens are white space, and U+2028 and U+2029 are not, as in V8.
entries.rootCause: DateParse scanned the UTF-8 bytes of its argument, a rule written for a header ByteString, so a U+00A0 or U+FEFF between date tokens (two bytes) made a timestamp NaN where V8 treats it as one white space unit; session and crash-log timestamps (session-manager.ts:795, crash-log) are full JavaScript strings. DateParse now scans utf16.Encode of the string, DateParseHeader keeps the byte rule for the Last-Modified header (remote_catalog_provider). V8's keyword scan stops only at IsWhiteSpace, so U+2028/U+2029 start a keyword and invalidate the date, and its white space token is one unit.
entries.releaseNote: Session and crash timestamps are read like Date.parse of a JavaScript string: U+00A0 and U+FEFF between tokens are white space, and U+2028 and U+2029 are not, as in V8.

It found CommandDecl.Args ("argument hint shown in /help"): no SDK sends it, the host never read it, and Pi's registerCommand has no such option (command registration is name, description, getArgumentCompletions, handler). Deleted per the caller-free rule.

entries.releaseNote: On arm64 and other CPUs with a fused multiply-add, the cache-warming expected savings (shown by `/session`, passed to extensions and compared with the $0.05 threshold), the "Sign in with Radius" shimmer and the 3D easter egg's blocks flying home match Pi: each product is rounded before it is added, as JavaScript does. Before, they could differ from Pi in the last digit, which changed some shimmer colors.

entries.title: A single server-sent-event line larger than 32 MiB (for example a base64 image chunk) no longer fails the…
entries.symptom: A single server-sent-event line larger than 32 MiB (for example a base64 image chunk) no longer fails the stream with `token too long` on the providers that use PiG's SSE decoder.
entries.rootCause: An earlier change replaced the invented 32 MiB cap with math.MaxInt, so a server that never ends a line grows the buffer until the process runs out of memory. Pi is bounded: each of its SSE readers holds the line in a JavaScript string, and Node cannot make one longer than buffer.constants.MAX_STRING_LENGTH (2^29-24; the OpenAI SDK LineDecoder throws 'Cannot create a string longer than 0x1fffffe8 characters', string buffers throw 'RangeError: Invalid string length'). sseLineLimit is that bound.
entries.releaseNote: A single server-sent-event line larger than 32 MiB (for example a base64 image chunk) no longer fails the stream with `token too long` on the providers that use PiG's SSE decoder. A line is now bounded where Pi's runtime bounds it, at Node's maximum string length (512 MiB), so a server that never ends a line cannot exhaust memory (D134).

entries.title: Markdown rendering follows Pi for lines made only of Unicode spaces (U+00A0, U+3000, U+2003 and the others…

entries.rootCause: Go's strings.TrimSpace strips U+0085 and keeps U+FEFF; JavaScript's trim() does the opposite, and marked's blank line, /^[ \t]*$/, is neither: a line of U+00A0, U+3000, U+2003 or U+2028 is text. Pig used TrimSpace for Pi's `text.trim() === ""` and for blank lines: Text rendered a BOM-only string as a row where Pi renders nothing, an assistant text block of U+FEFF was shown, the model selector took `<U+0085>d` as a prefix of "default", and a full-width space line (common between CJK paragraphs) ended a paragraph, a code block, a table or a heading's spacing where Pi keeps it as text.

entries.title: Provider request bodies write a lone UTF-16 surrogate as its escape, as `JSON.stringify` does, instead of…
entries.symptom: Provider request bodies write a lone UTF-16 surrogate as its escape, as `JSON.stringify` does, instead of U+FFFD for each byte of its Go form.
entries.rootCause: marshalRequestBody used encoding/json, which writes U+FFFD for each of the three WTF-8 bytes a Go string holds for a lone UTF-16 surrogate, where JSON.stringify writes the unit's escape. Pi leaves some strings unsanitized (the Codex instructions, openai-codex-responses.ts:552; an assistant message's reasoning fields), so PiG sanitized the first and corrupted the second. A body with a U+FFFD character is now encoded with the JSON.stringify encoder (jsstring.MarshalJSON), also inside the request types' own MarshalJSON; any other body encodes as before, so the request allocation gates are unchanged.
entries.releaseNote: Provider request bodies write a lone UTF-16 surrogate as its escape, as `JSON.stringify` does, instead of U+FFFD for each byte of its Go form. It matters for the strings Pi does not sanitize: the Codex `instructions`, now sent as Pi sends them, and the reasoning fields of an assistant message. A body with no U+FFFD character encodes as before.

entries.title: Without `HOME` set, the project trust check takes the home directory from the user database, as Pi's…
entries.symptom: Without `HOME` set, the project trust check takes the home directory from the user database, as Pi's `os.homedir()` does, instead of treating the working directory as the home directory.
entries.rootCause: hasTrustRequiringProjectResources canonicalizes process.env.HOME || homedir() (trust-manager.ts:187), and Node's os.homedir() reads the user database when HOME is unset or empty. entries.title: A Session listener that queues more messages than the Session's event buffer holds (64 by default), while it…
entries.symptom: A Session listener that queues more messages than the Session's event buffer holds (64 by default), while it runs on the goroutine that emitted its event, publishes its `queue_update` events in order.
entries.rootCause: The Session's event goroutine waited for execMu, a sync.Mutex, while a producer ran a callback inline under it. testing/synctest does not count a Mutex waiter as durably blocked, so synctest.Wait never returned while the callback was held: TestSessionObservationCloseJoinsClaimedCallback hung on its first run (the executor's shutdown waited for execMu), and TestCompactionFailureWaitsForEndListeners needed a synctest.Wait before compaction to dodge the same wait. execMu is now a lock whose waiters block on a channel receive; taking a free lock is one atomic add. The compaction test's workaround is removed.
entries.releaseNote: A Session listener that queues more messages than the Session's event buffer holds (64 by default), while it runs on the goroutine that emitted its event, publishes its `queue_update` events in order. An update could reach `Events` ahead of the one published just before it, so a subscriber saw a queue with one message too many. Every event published after such a burst now runs after it.

entries.title: Markdown resolves link reference definitions as Pi does: `[text][label]`, `[label][]` and `[label]` link to a…
entries.symptom: Markdown resolves link reference definitions as Pi does: `[text][label]`, `[label][]` and `[label]` link to a `[label]: url` defined anywhere in the message, and the definition line is no longer printed.
entries.rootCause: Markdown now ports marked 18.0.11's link reference definitions. The def block tokenizer runs after HTML blocks. Definitions go into a links map for the whole document, where the first definition of a tag wins. Reference, collapsed and shortcut links resolve against that map, and references to defined tags are masked for emphasis, including the link-in-text check. marked registers every definition before it lexes any inline text. So a document whose definition follows a "[" is rendered a second time with the full map. A definition renders no lines, as in Pi: blanks around it are kept, and text that renders nothing returns [""].
entries.releaseNote: Markdown resolves link reference definitions as Pi does: `[text][label]`, `[label][]` and `[label]` link to a `[label]: url` defined anywhere in the message, and the definition line is no longer printed. A list item whose text starts more than four spaces after its marker, as after a tab, renders as an indented code block.

entries.title: PiG opens a session file that holds a valid JSON line that is not an entry (an array, `true`, a string) or an…
entries.symptom: PiG opens a session file that holds a valid JSON line that is not an entry (an array, `true`, a string) or an entry whose `id` or `parentId` is not a string, as Pi does, instead of failing with `json: cannot unmarshal … SessionEntryBase`.
entries.rootCause: - sessionentry keeps an id or parentId that is not a string as the key of its JavaScript value. The key starts with a 0xFF byte, which no decoded string holds. An absent id or parentId is undefined, and a null id is null. Each parsed object or array gets a key of its own, because Map compares objects by identity. - Truthy is JavaScript truthiness. - ValueJSON writes the value back. A child's parentId is that value, and is omitted when undefined. - WireID is the leaf as a host-call string. - A LazyEntry keeps the keys it was indexed with. - The load no longer re-decodes the base of an undescribed record. Its leaf is the record's id, or null when that id is null. - getBranch, the context…
entries.userImpact: An operation failed or was rejected
entries.releaseNote: PiG opens a session file that holds a valid JSON line that is not an entry (an array, `true`, a string) or an entry whose `id` or `parentId` is not a string, as Pi does, instead of failing with `json: cannot unmarshal … SessionEntryBase`. The leaf, the branch, the context and the `parentId` of the next entry follow Pi: after a line with no `id` the next entry has no `parentId` member, after an entry whose `id` is `5` it has `"parentId":5`, and a falsy `parentId` ends a branch.

entries.symptom: Concurrent calls prepared side by side.
entries.rootCause: Pi's createPhotonImages runs prepare's synchronous work on the calling thread, so calls are prepared one after another in call order. The turn-taking queue moves from node's Worker false path into durable/images (sequential.go) around the native preparer, and node's Worker false returns CreatePhotonImages again, so the order lives in one place. entries.releaseNote: `durable/images.CreatePhotonImages`, and `durable/images/node.CreateNodePhotonImages` with `Worker: false`, which returns it, prepare images one at a time in call order on the caller's goroutine, as Pi's `createPhotonImages` does on its calling thread. Before, concurrent calls prepared side by side. A caller whose context is cancelled while it waits returns the context's error and does not hold up or reorder the calls after it.

entries.rootCause: A real-binary test runs print, print --no-session, JSON and RPC modes in a project whose only configuration is a project mcp.json with a stdio server. entries.title: A restarted extension, isolated or in a recovered packed cell, now offers the commands, flags, shortcuts and…
entries.symptom: A restarted extension, isolated or in a recovered packed cell, now offers the commands, flags, shortcuts and tools its new process registered; before, it kept the first registration's.
entries.rootCause: The register message carried a command argument hint (`args`, sent only by the Node runtime) and a per-handler `can_block` flag (sent by Node, Python and Rust). The host read neither, and Pi has neither concept: RegisteredCommand has no argument hint (types.ts:1541-1547, loader.ts:303) and every handler may return a result (runner.ts). The Go and Node SDK APIs never exposed can_block; Rust `on_event`/`on_event_result` and Python `on_event` did, so the SDK interfaces differed for no behaviour.
entries.releaseNote: A restarted extension, isolated or in a recovered packed cell, now offers the commands, flags, shortcuts and tools its new process registered; before, it kept the first registration's. Shortcuts keep their registration order.

entries.title: SDK: `Session.Dispose` now releases the Session as Pi's `dispose` does
entries.symptom: SDK: `Session.Dispose` now releases the Session as Pi's `dispose` does.
entries.rootCause: Pi's AgentSession.dispose (agent-session.ts:1389-1416) is for "when completely done with the session". It drops every listener and disconnects from the agent, so nothing of the Session stays live. PiG's Dispose cleared the listeners but left two things running until Close: - the event forwarder goroutine: the Events stream stayed open, and with no reader, producers blocked once the buffers filled; - the model registry observer. The services outlive a Session across replacement, so the registry observer kept a disposed Session reachable. An embedder that ends a Session with Dispose alone, as with Pi, leaked both.
entries.releaseNote: SDK: `Session.Dispose` now releases the Session as Pi's `dispose` does. Its `Events` stream closes, publishing and flushing events stop waiting, and the model registry no longer keeps a disposed Session reachable.

entries.rootCause: - nodeurl.Parse is `new URL(raw)` without a base for any scheme (protocol, hostname, encoded query): special schemes through the WHATWG special authority, file through the file parser (localhost is empty), other schemes through the non-special authority, host and port states (forbidden host code points, IPv6, port digits and 65535, credentials or port without a host) and the opaque-host percent-encoding. - parseAuthorizationInput (anthropic.ts:29, openai-codex.ts:69, openrouter.ts:30) and Copilot's normalizeDomain (github-copilot.ts:41) used Go's url.Parse for schemes other than http/https: ws/wss/ftp/file and custom schemes accepted ports above 65535, '<' in a host, 'u@' without a host…
entries.userImpact: An operation failed or was rejected
entries.releaseNote: GitHub Copilot login reads an enterprise domain the way Pi does: an IPv6 host keeps its brackets, an internationalized name becomes its `xn--` form, a numeric host is normalized (`1.2.3` is `1.2.0.3`) or refused when out of range, a backslash ends the host, and a port above 65535 refuses the domain. A domain given as a URL of a scheme other than `http`, `https`, `ws`, `wss` or `ftp` keeps its host as `new URL` reports it: the case as written, non-ASCII characters percent-encoded, and an empty host for `file://localhost`. The Copilot token's `proxy-ep=` claim is found anywhere in the token and used as written, as Pi does, instead of only at the start of a `;`-separated part and trimmed.

entries.title: Pasting an OAuth authorization into the Anthropic, OpenAI Codex or OpenRouter login now reads it the way Pi…
entries.symptom: Pasting an OAuth authorization into the Anthropic, OpenAI Codex or OpenRouter login now reads it the way Pi does.
entries.rootCause: - nodeurl.Parse is `new URL(raw)` without a base for any scheme (protocol, hostname, encoded query): special schemes through the WHATWG special authority, file through the file parser (localhost is empty), other schemes through the non-special authority, host and port states (forbidden host code points, IPv6, port digits and 65535, credentials or port without a host) and the opaque-host percent-encoding. - parseAuthorizationInput (anthropic.ts:29, openai-codex.ts:69, openrouter.ts:30) and Copilot's normalizeDomain (github-copilot.ts:41) used Go's url.Parse for schemes other than http/https: ws/wss/ftp/file and custom schemes accepted ports above 65535, '<' in a host, 'u@' without a host…
entries.userImpact: An operation failed or was rejected
entries.releaseNote: Pasting an OAuth authorization into the Anthropic, OpenAI Codex or OpenRouter login now reads it the way Pi does. A `code#state` paste keeps only the text up to the next `#` as the state. A bare query string with a leading `?`, a `;`, or a malformed `%` escape keeps the code instead of dropping it. A URL of any scheme that `new URL` refuses, such as one whose port is above 65535, is read as a plain code, not as a callback URL. An empty pasted state (`code#` or `state=`) reaches Anthropic's token request as an empty state, as in Pi, instead of being replaced by the login's own state.

entries.title: A streamed write card no longer slows down as its content grows
entries.symptom: A streamed write card no longer slows down as its content grows.
entries.rootCause: Since lw-tui2 every frame of a streaming write card encoded the whole partial argument object (ArgumentMembers) and decoded it twice, once for the header and once for the body, and the body split and normalised the whole content again: O(n) per frame, O(n^2) per stream (pauses write:400 6.6 -> 15 s CPU, 60 -> 395 MB own memory).
entries.releaseNote: A streamed write card no longer slows down as its content grows. Since streamed tool cards started drawing their partial arguments, every frame encoded the whole argument object and decoded it twice, and the write renderer split the whole content again, so a 400 KB write cost O(n²) (pauses write:400: 15 s CPU and 395 MB own memory, against 6.6 s and 60 MB before). The card now hands the built-in write renderer the object the streaming parser already holds, and the renderer extends its line count and highlighted lines from the previous frame, highlighting only the lines a frame draws. A frame allocates 77 KB at 400 KB received, as at 40 KB (3.1 MB before, 6.4 times the 40 KB frame). A settled write card keeps no highlighted copy of its content.

entries.title: A Go extension whose `go.mod` replace (or a Rust extension whose `pig-sdk` path dependency) points at an SDK…
entries.symptom: A Go extension whose `go.mod` replace (or a Rust extension whose `pig-sdk` path dependency) points at an SDK an earlier pig staged under its configuration root, for example through a link made with `pig reload --sdk-path go` before updating pig, now builds against the SDK the current pig staged. pig never deletes the SDK directories older versions staged, so such a link kept resolving and the extension compiled against the old SDK, failing at load with `decode register payload: json: unknown field ...`.
entries.rootCause: A go.mod replace (or Cargo path dependency) that resolves inside <config root>/state/pigsdk/ but outside the SDK this pig stages now points at an SDK an earlier pig staged; pig never deletes those directories, so a link made with `pig reload --sdk-path go` kept resolving after an update and the extension compiled against the old SDK, failing at register with `decode register payload: json: unknown field "can_block"` and making `pig extension upgrade` type-check against the same old SDK. Treat such a replace like a missing one in the packed, isolated and upgrade-analysis paths, Go and Rust; a replace anywhere else still wins.
entries.releaseNote: A Go extension whose `go.mod` replace (or a Rust extension whose `pig-sdk` path dependency) points at an SDK an earlier pig staged under its configuration root, for example through a link made with `pig reload --sdk-path go` before updating pig, now builds against the SDK the current pig staged. pig never deletes the SDK directories older versions staged, so such a link kept resolving and the extension compiled against the old SDK, failing at load with `decode register payload: json: unknown field ...`. An extension written for an older SDK now gets the `written for an older SDK` report instead. A replace that points anywhere else, such as your own SDK checkout or copy, still wins.

entries.title: A replacement request body from a `before_provider_request` hook on Anthropic Messages, and every OpenAI…
entries.symptom: A replacement request body from a `before_provider_request` hook on Anthropic Messages, and every OpenAI Codex WebSocket `response.create` message, now leave in Pi's member order (`type` first for the WebSocket message) instead of sorted keys.
entries.rootCause: The Anthropic replacement path split the body into a map and the WebSocket path built {type, ...requestBody} from a map, so both wrote sorted keys where Pi's JSON.stringify writes insertion order (type first, then the body's members; a cached continuation replaces input in place and adds previous_response_id last). Both now edit the body member by member (ai/ordered_json_object.go). Byte parity, no divergence.
entries.releaseNote: A replacement request body from a `before_provider_request` hook on Anthropic Messages, and every OpenAI Codex WebSocket `response.create` message, now leave in Pi's member order (`type` first for the WebSocket message) instead of sorted keys.

entries.title: `tool_search` and the Durable `searchTools()` ranker compute the same BM25 scores as Pi on arm64: the length…
entries.symptom: `tool_search` and the Durable `searchTools()` ranker compute the same BM25 scores as Pi on arm64: the length normalization `k1 * (1 - b + b * length / averageLength)` is rounded before the term count is added, instead of being fused into one multiply-add, so scores no longer differ from Pi's in the last bit and documents that tie in Pi keep their order (Pi 1.2.0 `tool-search/tool.ts` Bm25Ranker, `durable/src/search.ts` rankDocuments).
entries.rootCause: On arm64 the Go compiler fused k1*(...) + count into one FMADD, so tool_search and searchTools() scores differed from Pi's in the last bit and could reorder ties. TestToolSearchMatchesPi had 65 such mismatches.
entries.releaseNote: `tool_search` and the Durable `searchTools()` ranker compute the same BM25 scores as Pi on arm64: the length normalization `k1 * (1 - b + b * length / averageLength)` is rounded before the term count is added, instead of being fused into one multiply-add, so scores no longer differ from Pi's in the last bit and documents that tie in Pi keep their order (Pi 1.2.0 `tool-search/tool.ts` Bm25Ranker, `durable/src/search.ts` rankDocuments).

entries.title: The TypeScript extension runtime no longer depends on Node-only behaviour: its entry modules do not await the…
entries.symptom: The TypeScript extension runtime no longer depends on Node-only behaviour: its entry modules do not await the admission loop at top level (Bun never reaches `beforeExit` while an entry module's top-level await is pending, so the quit drain after RPC input ended hung), it hooks `v8.Serializer.prototype.writeValue` only where the runtime has it, it keeps a native method when the runtime froze built-ins, and it loads its lazy modules through one list that a bundling runtime can serve.
entries.rootCause: retryOnNextRuntime retried every error that was not a *LoadError, including a provider registration the host rejected after the register handshake; with a slot runtime selected the factory then ran again on the next runtime over its partial registration. It now retries only a *LoadError with a spawn, exit or register failure code, as its comment states. TestTypeScriptRuntimeRetriesOnlyStartFailures failed before the fix (provider registration error case).
entries.releaseNote: The TypeScript extension runtime no longer depends on Node-only behaviour: its entry modules do not await the admission loop at top level (Bun never reaches `beforeExit` while an entry module's top-level await is pending, so the quit drain after RPC input ended hung), it hooks `v8.Serializer.prototype.writeValue` only where the runtime has it, it keeps a native method when the runtime froze built-ins, and it loads its lazy modules through one list that a bundling runtime can serve. On Node, a serve failure still ends the extension process with exit code 1; a runtime process whose event loop empties while it waits for the next admission now exits 0 instead of Node's unsettled-top-level-await code 13 with its warning.

entries.title: A tool call whose arguments are not an object is written back to each provider as Pi writes it: Anthropic and…
entries.symptom: A tool call whose arguments are not an object is written back to each provider as Pi writes it: Anthropic and Google send `{}` for `null` (`arguments ?? {}`), Mistral sends `{}` for `null`, `0`, `false` and `""` (`arguments || {}`), Bedrock sends the value itself; a Gemini function call with `"args": null` is the empty object, and the agent proxy keeps Pi's `parseStreamingJson(...) || {}` and the streamed arguments of a `toolcall_end` that omits them.
entries.rootCause: An earlier change keeps a non-object parse result ([] null 5 "s") as Pi's parseStreamingJson returns it. The sites that read or write the value then passed it through verbatim, where Pi applies its own `?? {}` or `|| {}`. For null that is a regression: before the commit every site wrote {}. - Google ingest: google-generative-ai.ts:207 `args ?? {}`. `"args": null` now became the arguments null with delta "null". It is {} again (defaultNullishArguments). - Replay: anthropic-messages.ts:1444 `input: arguments ?? {}` and google-shared.ts:270 `args: arguments ?? {}` sent null. mistral-conversations.ts:849 `JSON.stringify(arguments || {})` sent "null", "0", "false" and `""`.…
entries.releaseNote: A tool call whose arguments are not an object is written back to each provider as Pi writes it: Anthropic and Google send `{}` for `null` (`arguments ?? {}`), Mistral sends `{}` for `null`, `0`, `false` and `""` (`arguments || {}`), Bedrock sends the value itself; a Gemini function call with `"args": null` is the empty object, and the agent proxy keeps Pi's `parseStreamingJson(...) || {}` and the streamed arguments of a `toolcall_end` that omits them.

entries.title: A `setTimeout(0)` or `setImmediate` callback that an extension queues while an RPC stdin command runs (a…
entries.symptom: A call that a Go, Rust or Python extension makes through a context whose request returned runs on arrival while another request of the extension is in flight, instead of waiting for a loop turn that waits for that request: a handler that kept an earlier request's context and awaited a call through it used to hang the run.
entries.rootCause: A handler that is still awaiting real I/O (a child process, a dialog) is not held back, because Pi's loop turns while it waits and runs the timer.
entries.releaseNote: A `setTimeout(0)` or `setImmediate` callback that an extension queues while an RPC stdin command runs (a `model_select` handler during `set_model`, say) now reaches the client after the command's response, as in Pi, instead of before it in about one run in ten. Pi runs the command's microtasks and writes its response before its loop runs a timer, so the Node runtime now holds its timer callbacks from the moment the host reads the command until the host has written the response, and the host waits for the runtime's acknowledgement of that hold before it sends the command's first event. A handler that is still awaiting real I/O (a child process, a dialog) is not held back, because Pi's loop turns while it waits and runs the timer. A call that a Go, Rust or Python extension makes through a context whose request returned runs on arrival while another request of the extension is in flight, instead of waiting for a loop turn that waits for that request: a handler that kept an earlier request's context and awaited a call through it used to hang the run.

entries.title: A subprocess extension's message, entry or tool renderer, or tool renderer resolver, that was busy past the…
entries.symptom: A subprocess extension's message, entry or tool renderer, or tool renderer resolver, that was busy past the five-second renderer inactivity boundary no longer leaves its card on the fallback until the next resize: the host asks again once the extension answers the abandoned request, and an extension that keeps missing the boundary is asked again after a backoff that starts at five seconds and doubles to one minute.
entries.rootCause: A resolve_tool_renderers request the renderer inactivity boundary abandoned recorded next() as the extension's answer, so the tool drew without the resolver's renderers for the rest of the session; Pi's resolvers answer synchronously. An abandoned resolution now records nothing, and renderRetry asks the extension again with the same next() (on the late answer after the first abandonment in a row, or after the backoff), on the goroutine group Shutdown joins. As for the first request, only an answer that differs from next() draws the tool's cards again. awaitRenderRetry also ends without a retry when the connection closes first.
entries.releaseNote: A subprocess extension's message, entry or tool renderer, or tool renderer resolver, that was busy past the five-second renderer inactivity boundary no longer leaves its card on the fallback until the next resize: the host asks again once the extension answers the abandoned request, and an extension that keeps missing the boundary is asked again after a backoff that starts at five seconds and doubles to one minute.

entries.title: A second `ctx.ui.custom` component opened while one is shown now opens over it at once, as in Pi, whether it…
entries.symptom: A subprocess extension's custom component waited until the shown one closed, and a subprocess custom component kept reading the keys while another custom component shown over it had focus.
entries.rootCause: Each SDK now holds the prompt the host rendered for the options the handler received and, once the options differ, asks the host to render them with renderSystemPrompt, reusing the result until they change again: - Go: data["systemPrompt"] is an *sdk.SystemPrompt (Get, MarshalJSON), since a map cannot run a getter; ctx.GetSystemPrompt() returns the same value. - Python: the event dict's "systemPrompt" and ctx.get_system_prompt() render. The Host answers renderSystemPrompt without a UI bridge too (an SDK session): the render is a pure function of the options the call carries. Callers of the Go string form move to Get(); the known gaps are deleted; pig-go.json is regenerated by gointerfaces.
entries.releaseNote: A second `ctx.ui.custom` component opened while one is shown now opens over it at once, as in Pi, whether it is an overlay or not and whichever extension process opens it. The component on top takes focus and the keys, and when it closes focus returns to the component below, which receives the next key. Before, a subprocess extension's custom component waited until the shown one closed, and a subprocess custom component kept reading the keys while another custom component shown over it had focus.

entries.rootCause: Owner decision 5 B. entries.releaseNote: A session keeps reading its history as it loaded it when another program rewrites, truncates, replaces or removes its session file, as Pi does. PiG reads history from a private snapshot of the session file. The snapshot is a file system clone where the file system supports one (Btrfs, XFS, APFS); elsewhere it is a copy that takes the file's size on disk. entries.userImpact: An operation failed or was rejected
entries.releaseNote: Two calls of a Go, Python or Rust extension tool in one assistant message that each open a dialog now behave as Pi's one thread makes them behave, as Node extensions already did: the dialogs open in call order (a port's second dialog could open first), and when the user answers them back to back the calls respond, and end, in the order of the answers. The SDKs keep these orders for the calls of one parallel batch, which the host now names on each `tool_call` request (`batch`); calls of other batches, other sessions' calls and tools that make no host call take no part and are never held. A handler that blocks on something other than a host call before its first host call holds the first dialogs of the later calls of its batch, while a call that awaits a host call such as `exec` before its dialog is overtaken by the later calls' dialogs, as in Pi, and a handler whose dialog was answered holds the later-answered handlers' responses until it returns or makes its next host call (recorded as divergence D187: Pi's single thread lets a call that awaits work the SDK cannot see be overtaken).

entries.title: Starting a child host could wait out its 30-second ready timeout ("child not ready in time") although the…
entries.symptom: Starting a child host could wait out its 30-second ready timeout ("child not ready in time") although the child was up.
entries.rootCause: Node cannot lose them, because an owner registers in the tick that creates the channel.
entries.releaseNote: Starting a child host could wait out its 30-second ready timeout ("child not ready in time") although the child was up. The Go port of Node's IPC channel read messages in its own goroutine and dropped any that arrived before its owner had registered a listener. Node cannot lose them, because an owner registers in the tick that creates the channel. A child that opened its channel after the parent's init message had been written could miss the init (so it never answered), and a manager descheduled between spawning the child and registering its control listener could miss the child's ready. The channel now keeps the messages received before its first listener and replays them to it in order, and a forked child instance does the same for its control listeners.

entries.title: Two calls of an extension tool in one assistant message now end in the order their tools answer, as Pi ends…
entries.symptom: Two calls of an extension tool in one assistant message now end in the order their tools answer, as Pi ends them.
entries.releaseNote: Two calls of an extension tool in one assistant message now end in the order their tools answer, as Pi ends them. In Pi, two tools that each wait on a dialog (or on timers of equal length) continue in the order their answers arrive, so `tool_execution_end` for the call whose dialog was answered first comes first. PiG woke the goroutines that waited for the two answers in no order, and on most runs the second call ended first, although its dialog was answered second. The host now records the order where the answers are read (a `tool_call` response from the extension's process, an RPC `extension_ui_response` line) and keeps it where the calls continue: the batch's `tool_execution_end` events, and the replies sent to the extension for its dialog calls. Tool-result messages still follow call order.

entries.releaseNote: `pig piglet verify <binary> --source <name|path>` and `pig piglet lineage <binary> --source <name|path>` report `Provenance: matches` for a Binary built from that unchanged source. entries.releaseNote: `go install github.com/MichaelKinsy/PiG/cmd/pig@main` builds again. The root `go.mod` required `extensions/sdk v0.5.0`, which lacks `Result.Drift`, `FileChange.Created` and `Skipped.Suggest` that `pig extension upgrade` uses, so building the module outside the workspace failed, and `make module-size` failed on every pull request. Between releases the root `go.mod` (and `piglets/standard` and `piglets/aot`) now require the SDK at the pseudo-version of the `main` commit that holds the API the root uses; the release replaces it with the tag. `make module-publication` accepts such a pseudo-version, and proves by downloading it into an empty cache, with the committed checksums, that the commit is public.

entries.title: A notification, status or message that an extension queues on `setImmediate` or `setTimeout(0)` from inside a…
entries.symptom: A notification, status or message that an extension queues on `setImmediate` or `setTimeout(0)` from inside a tool now reaches an RPC client after `agent_settled`, as Pi's loop does, instead of before `tool_execution_end`.
entries.rootCause: The Node runtime ran them as soon as the tool answered, because it is another process, and its host calls arrived mid-run.
entries.releaseNote: A notification, status or message that an extension queues on `setImmediate` or `setTimeout(0)` from inside a tool now reaches an RPC client after `agent_settled`, as Pi's loop does, instead of before `tool_execution_end`. Pi runs those callbacks when its event loop turns, which a run's chain of microtasks never gives it. The Node runtime ran them as soon as the tool answered, because it is another process, and its host calls arrived mid-run. The host now holds such calls while the RPC run chains microtasks and runs them in arrival order at the next real wait: a model response's I/O, a built-in tool's run, a dialog, a compaction or an auto-retry delay, or the end of `agent_settled`. A `process.nextTick` callback's notification follows the `tool_execution_end` of the tool that queued it, as in Pi, and the callbacks of a tool that returns while a sibling tool of its batch still runs reach the client right after its `tool_execution_end`.

entries.title: fix(ai): a lone surrogate in a content block stays one code unit, as in JSON.parse
entries.symptom: fix(ai): a lone surrogate in a content block stays one code unit, as in JSON.parse
entries.rootCause: UnmarshalContentBlock and ThinkingContent.UnmarshalJSON decoded with encoding/json, which turns a lone UTF-16 unit into U+FFFD, while the text shorthand of a tool result and the rest of the wire (extensions/sdk/json) keep it as the escape on the wire and WTF-8 in a Go string. A Node or Python tool that returned the block form lost the character; the shorthand kept it. Both forms, and every block a session line carries, now keep it. Also rows for unicode, NUL, U+2028, a 180 KB argument, and Scenario.Unrepresentable for a language limit (Rust strings cannot hold a lone surrogate). Tests: TestUnmarshalContentBlockKeepsALoneSurrogate, TestToolResultKeepsALoneSurrogateInEveryContentForm.

entries.symptom: fix(tui): Container.Render is safe beside a frame that borrows the window
entries.rootCause: An earlier change made a rebuild write into the array the render two back returned. Container.Render still cloned that array after releasing the lock, and it recycled arrays too. entries.rootCause: In a packed cell the host accepts members in order and serves a connection only after the members before it, so when the ui-peer member had registered first (thread order in the runner is not fixed) the rust-sdk-fixture factory's frontmatter.parse rode ui-peer's connection and waited for an answer the host would not send until the fixture had connected: a deadlock. strace of the stuck runner: the fixture thread sendto(fd of ui-peer's socket, frontmatter.parse) and never returned. Fix: running connections carry the socket they serve; with PIG_EXT_SOCKET set the helper uses the running extension on that socket and otherwise dials it (isolated extensions keep their own connection, an extension…
entries.releaseNote: A Go, Rust or Python extension that calls `parseFrontmatter` or `Date.parse` while its factory runs, in a runtime cell shared with other extensions, no longer waits forever when another member of the cell has already connected. The helper now uses the connection of the extension that owns the socket the runner names, and dials that socket when the extension has not connected yet, instead of reusing a sibling's connection that the host serves only later.

Every cell now registers "Label <name> <value>", which also proves the replacement carries its new label. - The in-process fixture's throw_probe returned "unused" although makeInprocFixture must match testfixture; it now throws the same messages and TestConformance_ThrownToolErrorMessagesAgreeAcrossSDKs runs the in-process Go reference too.

entries.symptom: On Windows, refreshing an MCP server's OAuth token no longer fails with `EPERM` when another `pig` process is still deleting the refresh lock.
entries.rootCause: The prune loop checks for cancellation only before each entry. A busy failure that arrived after the cancellation counted as skipped, and the last entry's classification could be cut short with nothing to remove, so the collection returned success and the automatic collector wrote its marker for a run that did not finish. The collection now checks for cancellation before it reports success.
entries.userImpact: An operation failed or was rejected
entries.releaseNote: On Windows, refreshing an MCP server's OAuth token no longer fails with `EPERM` when another `pig` process is still deleting the refresh lock. entries.title: Durable: opening a store that pi-durable 1.3.0 wrote no longer leaves you unable to go back to it
entries.symptom: Durable: opening a store that pi-durable 1.3.0 wrote no longer leaves you unable to go back to it.
entries.rootCause: PiG's Durable writes schema version 2, which pi-durable 1.3.0 refuses, and opening a version 1 store by file path upgraded it in place, so a user could not go back to the released Pi. The fix copies such a store to <path>.schema-<N>.bak (VACUUM INTO) before the upgrade; an earlier copy is never replaced, and a failed copy fails the open.
entries.userImpact: An operation failed or was rejected
entries.releaseNote: Durable: opening a store that pi-durable 1.3.0 wrote no longer leaves you unable to go back to it. PiG's Durable writes schema version 2, which no Pi release reads yet, and it upgraded the store in place. `driver.OpenHarness` and `node.OpenNodeSqliteStorage` now copy a store at an older schema version to `<path>.schema-1.bak` before upgrading it; pi-durable 1.3.0 opens that copy. An earlier copy is never replaced, and if the copy cannot be written the open fails and the store is left as it was. The copy is one extra file the size of the store, written once per older store (D188, #245; the commit that made the change calls it D186, its number before the renumber).

entries.title: A fused Go extension's `createLocalBashOperations().exec` (and `createLocalPowerShellOperations`) no longer…
entries.symptom: A fused Go extension's `createLocalBashOperations().exec` (and `createLocalPowerShellOperations`) no longer fails with "extension stopped while waiting for builtinTool.localExec response" when another extension in the same process stops while the command runs; a command past its `timeout` rejects with Pi's `timeout:<seconds>`.
entries.rootCause: localShellExec has no Context, so it sent builtinTool.localExec over runningExtension()'s connection: the first running extension in the process. A fused extension shares the process with every other fused extension, so a command with a timeout ended with "extension stopped while waiting for builtinTool.localExec response" when that extension stopped while the command ran, where Pi's exec rejects with "timeout:<seconds>" and depends on no extension.
entries.userImpact: An operation failed or was rejected
entries.releaseNote: A fused Go extension's `createLocalBashOperations().exec` (and `createLocalPowerShellOperations`) no longer fails with "extension stopped while waiting for builtinTool.localExec response" when another extension in the same process stops while the command runs; a command past its `timeout` rejects with Pi's `timeout:<seconds>`. The call has no `Context`, so it was sent over the connection of the first running extension in the process, and ended with that extension, whichever made the call. The host now runs the command for a fused extension directly, as it already does for the other helpers that have no `Context`, so the command depends on no extension, as Pi's exec depends on none.

entries.title: fix(codingagent): one owner-overflow forwarder at a time; the drain test waits for it, not for the flag's…
entries.symptom: fix(codingagent): one owner-overflow forwarder at a time; the drain test waits for it, not for the flag's early read
entries.rootCause: forwardOwnerOverflow removed the last task, released the lock, and only then took it again to see the overflow empty and clear ownerOverflowActive. A post the owner loop made in that gap (its queue still full) found the overflow empty, started a second forwarder and queued its task; both forwarders then sent the same task, which ran twice, and the second popped an empty overflow (index out of range in a background goroutine). The forwarder now leaves in the critical section that removes the last task and clears the flag, so a post that finds the overflow empty finds no forwarder.

entries.title: Migrating a version 1 session file that holds a line parsing to a number, string, array or `true` no longer…

entries.rootCause: Pi keeps whatever JSON.parse returns for a session-file line (session-manager.ts parseSessionEntryLine). migrateV1ToV2 gives every record after the header an id and a parent: an array takes the id as an unserialized property and the chain goes through it, a number, string or boolean throws the strict-mode TypeError.

Like Pi, an array record stays as written and still takes a place in the migration's id chain, and a number, string or boolean record stops the migration with the same `Cannot create property 'id'` error Pi throws.

entries.title: Anthropic and Bedrock assistant messages write `providerThinkingLevel` after `model`, and write…
entries.symptom: Anthropic and Bedrock assistant messages write `providerThinkingLevel` after `model`, and write `cacheWrite1h` and `reasoning` after `cost` in `usage`, as Pi does.
entries.rootCause: Pi passes a tool's parameters object through to the body (openai-completions.ts convertTools :1506-1514, openai-responses-shared.ts :386-390), so JSON.stringify writes the schema's members in declaration order; a strict schema is the same object rebuilt member by member (constrained-sampling.ts makeJsonSchemaNodeStrict: required, then additionalProperties are assigned after the existing members, and an optional property becomes {anyOf: [property, {type: "null"}]}). PiG copied ToolSchema.Parameters as a map[string]any and dropped the recorded parameterOrder, so every schema object was written in sorted order.
entries.releaseNote: Anthropic and Bedrock assistant messages write `providerThinkingLevel` after `model`, and write `cacheWrite1h` and `reasoning` after `cost` in `usage`, as Pi does.

entries.title: Installing a Package or Piglet from a local `git:file://` source on Windows no longer fails with `fatal…
entries.symptom: Installing a Package or Piglet from a local `git:file://` source on Windows no longer fails with `fatal: '$GIT_DIR' too big`.
entries.rootCause: A file:// source checked out to <root>/localhost/<whole absolute path>, doubling its length; Git for Windows then failed with "$GIT_DIR too big" whatever core.longpaths says. A file:// source now checks out to <host>/<12 hex of sha256(absolute path)>/<basename>. Sources Pi accepts keep Pi's layout. Older nested file:// checkouts are not reused.
entries.userImpact: An operation failed or was rejected
entries.releaseNote: Installing a Package or Piglet from a local `git:file://` source on Windows no longer fails with `fatal: '$GIT_DIR' too big`. A file URL now checks out to `<install root>/localhost/<12 hex of the path's sha256>/<basename>` instead of re-nesting the whole absolute path, which pushed `$GIT_DIR` past Git for Windows' own path limit that `core.longpaths` does not lift. Sources Pi accepts keep Pi's exact layout. A file URL checkout made by an earlier version is not reused and is cloned again.

entries.title: When an extension's `before_provider_request` handler replaces an Anthropic request, or a Codex WebSocket…

entries.rootCause: One part of is still missing there: writeJSONObjectMembers copied each value's text (json.Compact). The Codex WebSocket writer shares it; a body from marshalRequestBody is already canonical and takes the copy path.
entries.releaseNote: When an extension's `before_provider_request` handler replaces an Anthropic request, or a Codex WebSocket request carries raw JSON, nested values are written as Pi's `JSON.stringify` writes them after `JSON.parse`: `\u00e9` becomes `é`, and a nested object's repeated key keeps its first place with its last value. entries.title: A run that `sendMessage({ triggerTurn: true })` starts while idle emits `before_agent_start`, checks…
entries.symptom: A run that `sendMessage({ triggerTurn: true })` starts while idle emits `before_agent_start`, checks compaction first, applies the handlers' result and delivers pending `nextTurn` messages.
entries.rootCause: PiG did this only for idle triggerTurn custom messages (D139) and prepared a user prompt idle.
entries.releaseNote: A run that `sendMessage({ triggerTurn: true })` starts while idle emits `before_agent_start`, checks compaction first, applies the handlers' result and delivers pending `nextTurn` messages. The event carries `messageType` (`"user"` or `"custom"`) and, for a custom run, `message`. A user prompt's run, like a custom one, is busy from its start, as in Pi 1.2.0: a message sent while its compaction check and `before_agent_start` handlers run joins it, a prompt or `sendUserMessage` sent meanwhile must name `streamingBehavior`/`deliverAs`, bash results recorded meanwhile are appended after the handlers, and an abort aborts the run at `agent_start` instead of letting its request complete (Pi #5581, Pi PR #10739).

entries.title: Extensions' `ui_prompt_start` and `ui_prompt_end` notifications are recorded in order when the host is slow…
entries.symptom: Extensions' `ui_prompt_start` and `ui_prompt_end` notifications are recorded in order when the host is slow to apply the start event's `ctx.ui.notify`: the dialog's answer is no longer let through, and the end event no longer sent, before the handler's own host call has applied.
entries.rootCause: A runtime reports the suspension of a handler that waits for a host call before it sends the call. A start notification applied late (a stalled goroutine on a loaded machine) was recorded after the answers settled and the end event's notification, where Pi runs each handler's synchronous part before the prompting extension continues (TestConformance_ConcurrentDialogsAgreeAcrossSDKs/fused-go/last_in_first_out failed once in three full runs: the first ui_prompt event was the end).
entries.releaseNote: Extensions' `ui_prompt_start` and `ui_prompt_end` notifications are recorded in order when the host is slow to apply the start event's `ctx.ui.notify`: the dialog's answer is no longer let through, and the end event no longer sent, before the handler's own host call has applied. A blocked-on-a-host-call report from an extension runtime admitted the UI prompt drain as soon as it was read, while the call it announced was still queued; the admission now waits for that call.

entries.title: Interactive startup writes the terminal color query before its first frame, as Pi does: starting the renderer…
entries.symptom: Interactive startup writes the terminal color query before its first frame, as Pi does: starting the renderer only requests the first frame, which paints while startup waits for the terminal's colors.
entries.rootCause: Pi's TUI.start() requests the first frame instead of painting it, and init() writes the color query in applyFromSettings() before the deferred frame runs at await waitForTerminalColors(). Init now mounts the layout, starts the renderer with a requested frame (TuiAltScreen.StartRequestingRender in fullscreen), and the color wait serves scheduled renders, so the frame paints during the wait. A live tui-mode switch still paints at once.
entries.releaseNote: Interactive startup writes the terminal color query before its first frame, as Pi does: starting the renderer only requests the first frame, which paints while startup waits for the terminal's colors. In fullscreen the alternate screen is still entered first. The color round trip is now under way when the editor first shows, so input typed at the first frame waits on the same startup work as in Pi.

entries.title: A Node extension that calls `pi.appendEntry` many times in one handler no longer slows down with the size of…
entries.symptom: A Node extension that calls `pi.appendEntry` many times in one handler no longer slows down with the size of the session: each append now costs the same, as in Pi.
entries.rootCause: Upstream SessionManager.appendCustomEntry pushes the entry, sets byId and moves the leaf: O(1). entries.title: After `await ctx.reload()`, a command's captured `pi` and `ctx` now throw Pi's stale message for every…
entries.symptom: Members an SDK answers locally, such as `ctx.cwd`, `getFlag`, `getCommands`, `getThinkingLevel`, `getSystemPrompt` and `isProjectTrusted`, kept answering for the replaced extension instance.
entries.rootCause: retireGeneration now sends the invalidate notify (Pi's stale message) to a replaced generation whose stop a running command defers, under retirementMu, so it precedes both the reply to the reload and the deferred stop's shutdown. An immediately stopped generation needs none (its runtime invalidates as its connection ends); sending it there deadlocked a retained Node reload whose invalidation unsubscribes its shared-bus listeners while the reload waits for the process to close. The Go SDK's Context.Reload waits for the notifies queued before its result, as AppendEntry does, because its main loop applies notifies after the read loop routed the result.
entries.releaseNote: After `await ctx.reload()`, a command's captured `pi` and `ctx` now throw Pi's stale message for every member, in every SDK (Node, Go, Python and Rust). Before, members an SDK answers locally, such as `ctx.cwd`, `getFlag`, `getCommands`, `getThinkingLevel`, `getSystemPrompt` and `isProjectTrusted`, kept answering for the replaced extension instance.

entries.title: A `delta.Tracker` no longer keeps memory alive that Pi's tracker releases
entries.symptom: A `delta.Tracker` no longer keeps memory alive that Pi's tracker releases.
entries.rootCause: - AssertValidOp never checked path safety: it accepted [-1], [1.5], [true], [null] and nested segments that Pi's assertPathArg rejects. - Its messages carried an "invalid delta operation: " prefix and wrong names ("t payload" for Pi's "t shape", "invalid ... path" for "path is empty"). - ApplyImmutable rejected a numeric segment on an object; Pi sets that key: applyImmutable({a:1}, [["s",[1],2]]) is {"1":2,"a":1}. - The public path_error test expected ["a","b","c"] where Pi reports the unresolvable container ["a","b"].
entries.releaseNote: A `delta.Tracker` no longer keeps memory alive that Pi's tracker releases. A settled `Change`, a draft handle kept after its change settled, and a `Prepared` no longer keep the draft, the base revision or the `Tracker` alive. An aborted change no longer stays registered with its tracker until the next adoption, and an open change the caller drops is reclaimed. Each case is one of Pi's `retention.test.ts` scenarios.

entries.title: Replaying a thinking block that holds only U+FEFF drops it and one that holds only U+0085 keeps it, as…
entries.symptom: Replaying a thinking block that holds only U+FEFF drops it and one that holds only U+0085 keeps it, as JavaScript trim() decides in Pi.
entries.rootCause: Pi's transformMessages skips a thinking block whose text is empty after trim() (transform-messages.ts:111). Go's TrimSpace strips U+0085 and keeps U+FEFF, so a block of only U+FEFF was kept and replayed as text or thinking, and a block of only U+0085 was dropped, where Pi does the opposite. normalizeAssistantReplayBlocks now uses jsstring.Trim.
entries.releaseNote: Replaying a thinking block that holds only U+FEFF drops it and one that holds only U+0085 keeps it, as JavaScript trim() decides in Pi.

entries.title: `pig extension upgrade` no longer changes, breaks or rejects a Go extension that already builds against the…
entries.symptom: `pig extension upgrade` no longer changes, breaks or rejects a Go extension that already builds against the current SDK.
entries.rootCause: fmt.Println(ctx.ConfigHome()) compiles against the current SDK: the value and the error spread into ...any, so no compile error marks it and the error is printed instead of handled. Find a getter call that is the only argument of a variadic call (or print/println) syntactically, in files without compile errors too, and rewrite it as the other argument positions: hoist it and return the error, or list a ConfigHome whose function cannot return it. A non-variadic call whose parameters take the value and the error is the new shape and stays. The fixture test now also fails when a file with a golden source is not rewritten.
entries.userImpact: An operation failed or was rejected
entries.releaseNote: `pig extension upgrade` no longer changes, breaks or rejects a Go extension that already builds against the current SDK. A getter passed straight into a variadic call, such as `fmt.Println(ctx.GetActiveTools())`, is current code when the getter returned its error in the SDK the extension's `go.mod` requires, so it is left as it is. The upgrade now rewrites only `ConfigHome` calls of this kind, in extensions that require an SDK older than 0.5.0, and lists such a call rather than discard its error. A call whose parameter for the error has the type `error` stays. Rewriting one of these calls no longer also rewrites `ContextUsage.Tokens` and `Percent` uses that were already correct. A getter in a `select` case is listed instead of making the upgrade fail with `the rewrite does not parse`.

entries.title: A provider stream could stop for good, with the turn waiting for events that never came, when the goroutine…
entries.symptom: A provider stream could stop for good, with the turn waiting for events that never came, when the goroutine that reads the stream and the goroutine that runs the provider's response were scheduled against each other as the stream started.
entries.rootCause: changelog.d held 62 fragments in legacy.txt, which exempts them from the marker rule.
entries.releaseNote: A provider stream could stop for good, with the turn waiting for events that never came, when the goroutine that reads the stream and the goroutine that runs the provider's response were scheduled against each other as the stream started. The reader's goroutine could pick up a reaction loop that belonged to the response, run the reader's code beside a reaction that had not returned, and leave the stream's executor marked busy with nothing running. A goroutine now continues only a reaction loop its own turn holds, so no code runs beside a reaction and every stream ends. It stalled once in CI on Windows (`TestGoogleProviderStreamMatchesPi`); the same stall reproduces on macOS and Linux when the executor's lock hand-offs are delayed.
