entries.rootCause: A Node extension whose factory failed, because it has no default export or throws while initializing, could be reported as `connect:process_exited ... exit status 1` instead of Pi's "Extension does not export a valid factory function: <path>" or "Failed to load extension: <message>".

The extension's runtime reports that error over its socket and exits; on a loaded machine the host looked after the exit and chose between the connection and the exit by whichever it noticed first, which failed about 1 run in 20 of the upstream extension-discovery tests. The host now accepts the connection the extension made before it exited, in both a packed cell and an isolated process, and reports `process_exited` only for a process that never connected.

entries.releaseNote: A `--print` or `--mode json` run that SIGTERM or SIGHUP reaches while its bash tool is starting the shell no longer has a data race on `os.Stdout`. It now compares them with the files `os.Stdin`, `os.Stdout` and `os.Stderr` held when pig started, which stay open as before. The output and exit status are unchanged.

entries.title: fix(extension): hold the theme colors map the wire palette memo is keyed on
entries.symptom: fix(extension): hold the theme colors map the wire palette memo is keyed on
entries.rootCause: ActiveExtensionThemeWire identified the terminal-resolved colors by the address of the map theme.Colors returned, stored as a uintptr. The theme drops that map when the terminal's reported colors change, so the collector could free it and give its address to a later colors map with other values; the memo would then return the old palette and the state push would skip the theme as unchanged. The memo now holds the map it is keyed on, so the address cannot be reused while it identifies the palette.

entries.title: `pi.exec`'s `timeout` starts once the command has been spawned, as in Pi, so time spent finding and starting…
entries.symptom: `pi.exec`'s `timeout` starts once the command has been spawned, as in Pi, so time spent finding and starting the program no longer counts against it.
entries.rootCause: exec.ts:75 sets the timer after spawn has returned, so finding and starting the program does not count against options.timeout. ExecCommand started it before the PATH search and the fork, so a slow spawn (a long PATH, a loaded host) killed the child before it ran where Pi lets it finish.
entries.releaseNote: `pi.exec`'s `timeout` starts once the command has been spawned, as in Pi, so time spent finding and starting the program no longer counts against it.

entries.title: A task list item whose first line looks like a heading, quote, rule, bullet, fence, table row or HTML tag…
entries.symptom: A task list item whose first line looks like a heading, quote, rule, bullet, fence, table row or HTML tag renders that line as text, and a setext heading over it keeps the checkbox marker, as Pi does.
entries.rootCause: marked splits `[ ] ` into a checkbox token and lexes the rest of the first line as a text token, so `- [ ] # h`, `- [ ] > q`, `- [ ] ---`, `- [ ] - a`, a fence, a table row, a definition or an HTML tag renders as text, while the lines after it are lexed normally; a setext heading over the first line (`- [ ] t` / `===`) takes the marker into its text and the item has no checkbox. Pig stripped the marker and rendered the block. renderList now keeps the marker when setextHeadingEnd matches the original text, and otherwise lexes the first block with a leading control character that no block rule matches, removed from the rendered rows.
entries.releaseNote: A task list item whose first line looks like a heading, quote, rule, bullet, fence, table row or HTML tag renders that line as text, and a setext heading over it keeps the checkbox marker, as Pi does.

entries.title: A surrogate pair split across two concatenated string halves is written as its character in session files…
entries.symptom: A surrogate pair split across two concatenated string halves is written as its character in session files, extension frames and Durable records, as Pi's `JSON.stringify` writes it, instead of as two `\u` escapes.
entries.rootCause: Sibling of (durable/core/jv). The shared host/Go-SDK codec writes WTF-8 surrogate units as \u escapes; a high unit directly followed by a low unit (two WTF-8 halves concatenated in Go) is one code point in a JavaScript string, and JSON.stringify writes the character (node 24: JSON.stringify("\ud83d" + "\ude00") === '"😀"'). appendString now joins such a pair into its four-byte UTF-8; unpaired units stay escapes. This codec writes session entries (jsstring.MarshalJSON), extension frames and Durable storage.
entries.releaseNote: A surrogate pair split across two concatenated string halves is written as its character in session files, extension frames and Durable records, as Pi's `JSON.stringify` writes it, instead of as two `\u` escapes.

entries.title: A long session keeps less memory for each turn it has compacted away
entries.symptom: A long session keeps less memory for each turn it has compacted away.
entries.rootCause: A 21,000-turn RPC session with automatic compaction grew its live heap by 1.75 KiB per turn. Three parts of that were not entries Pi also keeps: - the /tree search text of an entry compaction moved out of the context was built at eviction (about 340 B per turn); it is now read from the entry's record on the first search, as after an open - the ai tool-call argument encoding cache kept the encodings of dropped calls until its 16 MiB limit (about 480 B per turn); an encoding is now released when its arguments are unreachable - agent.Recorder appended a duration per turn; it keeps the count and the last duration
entries.releaseNote: A long session keeps less memory for each turn it has compacted away. The `/tree` search text of an entry that compaction moves out of the context is no longer built and kept when the entry leaves memory: the first search reads it from the entry's record, as it already did after opening a session, and a session nobody searches keeps none. The cache of encoded tool-call arguments releases an encoding when the arguments it encodes are no longer reachable, where it kept the encodings of dropped calls until its 16 MiB limit. The agent's turn timer keeps the number of completed turns and the last duration instead of one duration per turn. In a 21,000-turn RPC session with automatic compaction on a 32k window, live heap growth falls from about 1.7 KiB per turn to the index of the session's entries (slots, compressed records, compaction entries), which Pi's in-memory session also keeps, as whole entries.
